translations.literal: Volume 143
translations.idiomatic: Volume 143

sentences.zh: 【齊紀九】 上章執徐，一年。

translations.literal: [Qi Records 9] Shangzhang Zhixu; one year.
translations.idiomatic: [Qi Records 9] Shangzhang Zhixu—one year.

sentences.zh: 東昏侯下永元二年（

translations.literal: Emperor Donghun, second year of Yongyuan (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Donghun, second year of Yongyuan (

sentences.zh: 庚辰，公元五零零年）

translations.literal: gengchen, the year 500 CE)
translations.idiomatic: gengchen, the year 500 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，元會，帝食後方出；

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, at the New Year's assembly, the emperor came out only after he had eaten;
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, at the New Year's court assembly, the emperor did not appear until after he had finished his meal;

sentences.zh: 朝賀裁竟，即還殿西序寢。

translations.literal: as soon as the congratulatory rites barely ended, he at once returned to sleep in the western wing of the hall.
translations.idiomatic: and as soon as the congratulatory rites were barely over, he went straight back to the western wing of the palace to sleep.

sentences.zh: 自巳至申，百僚陪位，皆僵仆饑甚。

translations.literal: From si hour to shen hour, the hundred officials standing in attendance all stiffly collapsed, famished in the extreme.
translations.idiomatic: From the si hour until the shen hour, the officials who had to stand in attendance were stiff with hunger and exhaustion.

sentences.zh: 比起就會，匆遽而罷。

translations.literal: When he rose and came to the assembly, it was hurried and then dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: When he finally rose and came to the assembly, the ceremony was rushed through and dismissed.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，魏大赦，改元景明。

translations.literal: On yisi, Wei proclaimed a general amnesty and changed the era name to Jingming.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi, Northern Wei proclaimed a general amnesty and changed the era name to Jingming.

sentences.zh: 豫州刺史裴叔業聞帝數誅大臣，心不自安；

translations.literal: Inspector of Yu Province Pei Shuye heard that the emperor repeatedly executed great ministers and was ill at ease in his heart;
translations.idiomatic: Pei Shuye, inspector of Yu Province, heard that the emperor was repeatedly executing senior ministers and grew uneasy;

sentences.zh: 登壽陽城，北望肥水，謂部下曰：「卿等欲富貴乎？

translations.literal: He ascended Shouyang city, looked north toward the Fei River, and said to his subordinates: "Do you gentlemen wish for wealth and honor?
translations.idiomatic: He climbed the walls of Shouyang, gazed north across the Fei River, and said to his officers: "Do you want wealth and rank?

sentences.zh: 我能辦之！」

translations.literal: I can arrange it!"
translations.idiomatic: I can get it for you!"

sentences.zh: 及除南兗州，意不樂內徙。

translations.literal: When he was transferred to Nan Yan Province, his mind was not pleased at an inward move.
translations.idiomatic: When he was reassigned to Nan Yan Province, he was unhappy at being moved inland.

sentences.zh: 會陳顯達反。

translations.literal: It happened that Chen Xianda rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: About this time Chen Xianda rose in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 叔業遣司馬遼東李元護將兵救建康，實持兩端；

translations.literal: Shuye sent his marshal Li Yuanhu of Liaodong to lead troops to rescue Jiankang, but in fact he held to both sides;
translations.idiomatic: Shuye sent his marshal Li Yuanhu of Liaodong with troops to relieve Jiankang, but in fact he kept his options open;

sentences.zh: 顯達敗而還。

translations.literal: Xianda was defeated and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Xianda was defeated and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 朝廷疑叔業有異志，叔業亦遣使參察建康消息，眾論益疑之。

translations.literal: The court suspected Shuye of disloyal intent; Shuye also sent envoys to investigate news from Jiankang, and public opinion grew ever more suspicious of him.
translations.idiomatic: The court began to suspect that Shuye harbored disloyal designs, and Shuye in turn sent agents to gauge the situation in Jiankang, which only deepened the suspicions against him.

sentences.zh: 叔業兄子植、颺、粲皆為直閣，在殿中，懼，棄母奔壽陽，說叔業以朝廷必相掩襲，宜早為計。

translations.literal: Shuye's elder brother's sons Zhi, Yang, and Can were all direct attendants in the hall; in fear they abandoned their mother and fled to Shouyang, urging Shuye that the court would surely launch a surprise attack and that he ought to plan early.
translations.idiomatic: Shuye's nephews Zhi, Yang, and Can, who served as palace attendants, were terrified; they abandoned their mother and fled to Shouyang, warning Shuye that the court would surely move against him by surprise and that he should act at once.

sentences.zh: 徐世檦等以叔業在邊，急則引魏自助，力未能制，白帝遣叔業宗人中書舍人長穆宣旨，許停本任。

translations.literal: Xu Shizhen and others, considering that with Shuye on the frontier, in urgency he would call on Wei for aid and they lacked strength to control him, reported to the emperor and sent Shuye's clansman Secretariat Attendant Chang Mu to announce the imperial will, permitting him to remain in his original post.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Shizhen and others, fearing that Shuye on the frontier might summon Wei to his aid if pressed and that they lacked the force to restrain him, persuaded the emperor to send Shuye's kinsman Chang Mu of the Secretariat to announce that he might keep his current post.

sentences.zh: 叔業猶憂畏，而植等說之不已。

translations.literal: Shuye still worried and feared, while Zhi and the others urged him without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Shuye remained anxious, and Zhi and his brothers kept pressing him.

sentences.zh: 叔業遣親人馬文范至襄陽，問蕭衍以自安之計，曰：「天下大勢可知，恐無復自存之理。

translations.literal: Shuye sent his close associate Ma Wenfan to Xiangyang to ask Xiao Yan for a plan to secure himself, saying: "The great trend of the realm can be known; I fear there is no longer any principle by which to preserve myself.
translations.idiomatic: Shuye sent his confidant Ma Wenfan to Xiangyang to ask Xiao Yan how he might save himself, saying: "The drift of affairs is clear enough; I doubt I can survive much longer on my own.

sentences.zh: 不若回面向北，不失作河南公。」

translations.literal: It would be better to turn and face north; one would not fail to become Duke of Henan."
translations.idiomatic: Better to turn north and at least keep the title of Duke of Henan."

sentences.zh: 衍報曰：「群小用事，豈能及遠！

translations.literal: Yan replied: "Petty men hold power—how can they reach far!
translations.idiomatic: Yan replied: "Petty men are running things—how far can their reach extend?

sentences.zh: 計慮回惑，自無所成，唯應送家還都以安慰之。

translations.literal: Their schemes are confused and turning; of themselves they accomplish nothing. You should only send your family back to the capital to reassure them.
translations.idiomatic: Their plots are muddled and self-defeating. You should send your family back to the capital to reassure the court.

sentences.zh: 若意外相逼，當勒馬步二萬直出橫江，以斷其後，則天下之事，一舉可定。

translations.literal: If by unexpected circumstance you are pressed, you should muster twenty thousand horse and foot to strike straight out from Hengjiang and cut their rear; then the affairs of the realm can be settled in one move.
translations.idiomatic: If they should press you unexpectedly, muster twenty thousand horse and foot, march straight from Hengjiang, and cut them off from behind—the whole affair could be settled in a single stroke.

sentences.zh: 若欲北向，彼必遣人相代，以河北一州相處，河南公寧可復得邪！

translations.literal: If you wish to turn north, they will surely send someone to replace you and grant you but one province north of the river—how could you ever again obtain the title Duke of Henan!
translations.idiomatic: If you go north, they will send someone to replace you and give you only a single province north of the Yellow River—how could you ever again be Duke of Henan?

sentences.zh: 如此，則南歸之望絕矣。」

translations.literal: In this way, the hope of returning south would be cut off."
translations.idiomatic: That would end any hope of returning to the south."

sentences.zh: 叔業沉疑未決，乃遣其子芬之入建康為質，亦遣信詣魏豫州刺史薛真度，問以入魏可不之宜。

translations.literal: Shuye sank in doubt and could not decide; he then sent his son Fenzhi into Jiankang as a hostage, and also sent a message to Wei Inspector of Yu Province Xue Zhendu to ask whether entering Wei was feasible or not.
translations.idiomatic: Shuye hesitated, unable to decide. He sent his son Fenzhi to Jiankang as a hostage and also wrote to Xue Zhendu, Wei's inspector of Yu Province, to ask whether defecting to Wei was advisable.

sentences.zh: 真度勸其早降，曰：「若事迫而來，則功微賞薄矣。」

translations.literal: Zhendu urged him to surrender early, saying: "If you come when affairs are already pressing, then merit will be slight and rewards thin."
translations.idiomatic: Zhendu urged him to surrender promptly, saying: "If you wait until you are forced to it, your merit will be small and your reward meager."

sentences.zh: 數遣密信，往來相應和。

translations.literal: He repeatedly sent secret letters, going back and forth in mutual response.
translations.idiomatic: They exchanged many secret messages in concert.

sentences.zh: 建康人傳叔業叛者不已，芬之懼，復奔壽陽。

translations.literal: People in Jiankang kept spreading word that Shuye had rebelled without cease; Fenzhi was afraid and again fled to Shouyang.
translations.idiomatic: Rumors in Jiankang that Shuye had defected would not die down; Fenzhi, frightened, fled back to Shouyang.

sentences.zh: 叔業遂遣芬之及兄女婿杜陵韋伯昕奉表降魏。

translations.literal: Shuye thereupon sent Fenzhi and his elder brother's son-in-law Wei Boxin of Duling to present a memorial surrendering to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Shuye then sent Fenzhi and his brother-in-law Wei Boxin of Duling with a memorial offering surrender to Wei.

sentences.zh: 丁未，魏遣驃騎大將軍彭城王勰、東騎將軍王肅帥步騎十萬赴之；

translations.literal: On dingwei, Wei sent Grand General of Agile Cavalry Prince Xie of Pengcheng and General of the Eastern Horse Wang Su to command one hundred thousand foot and horse to hurry there;
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei, Wei dispatched Prince Xie of Pengcheng, grand general of agile cavalry, and Wang Su, general of the eastern horse, with one hundred thousand infantry and cavalry to support him;

sentences.zh: 以叔業為使持節、都督豫、雍等五州諸軍事、征南將軍、豫州刺史，封蘭陵郡公。

translations.literal: Shuye was made bearer of the staff, commander of all military affairs in Yu, Yong, and five other provinces, General Who Subdues the South, Inspector of Yu Province, and enfeoffed as Duke of Lanling.
translations.idiomatic: and appointed Shuye bearer of the staff, commander of military affairs in Yu, Yong, and five other provinces, general who subdues the south, inspector of Yu Province, and duke of Lanling.

sentences.zh: 庚午，下詔討叔業。

translations.literal: On gengwu, an edict was issued to campaign against Shuye.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu, the court issued an edict to campaign against Shuye.

sentences.zh: 二月，丙戌，以衛尉蕭懿為豫州刺史。

translations.literal: In the second month, on bingxu, Xiao Yi of the Guard Command was made Inspector of Yu Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on bingxu, Xiao Yi of the Guard Command was appointed inspector of Yu Province.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，魏以彭城王勰為司徒，領揚州刺史，鎮壽陽。

translations.literal: On wuxu, Wei made Prince Xie of Pengcheng Minister of Works, concurrently Inspector of Yang Province, and stationed him at Shouyang.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu, Wei made Prince Xie of Pengcheng minister of works, gave him concurrent charge of Yang Province, and posted him at Shouyang.

sentences.zh: 魏人遣大將軍李丑、楊大眼將二千騎入壽陽，又遣奚康生將羽林一千馳赴之。

translations.literal: The people of Wei sent Grand Generals Li Chou and Yang Dayan to lead two thousand horse into Shouyang, and also sent Xi Kangsheng to lead one thousand Forest Guards in rapid advance there.
translations.idiomatic: Wei sent the grand generals Li Chou and Yang Dayan with two thousand cavalry into Shouyang, and dispatched Xi Kangsheng with one thousand Forest Guards at full speed to join them.

sentences.zh: 大眼，難當之孫也。

translations.literal: Dayan was the grandson of Nandang.
translations.idiomatic: Dayan was a grandson of Nandang.

sentences.zh: 魏兵未渡淮，己亥，裴叔業病卒，僚佐多欲推司馬李元護監州，一二日謀不定。

translations.literal: Before Wei troops had crossed the Huai, on jihai Pei Shuye died of illness; his staff mostly wished to push Marshal Li Yuanhu to oversee the province, but for a day or two their plans were unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: Before Wei forces had crossed the Huai, on jihai Pei Shuye died of illness. Most of his staff wanted Li Yuanhu, the marshal, to take charge of the province, but for a day or two they could not settle on a plan.

sentences.zh: 前建安戍主安定席法友等以元護非其鄉曲，恐有異志，共推裴植監州，秘叔業喪問，教命處分，皆出於植。

translations.literal: The former garrison commander of Jian'an, Xi Fayou of Anding, and others, because Yuanhu was not of their native district and they feared disloyal intent, jointly pushed Pei Zhi to oversee the province; they concealed news of Shuye's death, and all orders and dispositions issued from Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Fayou of Anding, the former commander of the Jian'an garrison, and others, distrusting Yuanhu because he was not a fellow townsman and fearing treachery, backed Pei Zhi instead. They concealed Shuye's death, and all orders issued in his name came from Zhi.

sentences.zh: 奚康生至，植乃開門納魏兵，城庫管籥，悉付康生。

translations.literal: When Xi Kangsheng arrived, Zhi then opened the gates and admitted Wei troops; the city stores and keys were all handed over to Kangsheng.
translations.idiomatic: When Xi Kangsheng arrived, Zhi opened the gates and admitted the Wei troops, handing over the city treasury and all its keys to him.

sentences.zh: 康生集城內耆舊，宣詔撫賚之。

translations.literal: Kangsheng gathered the elders of the city, proclaimed the edict, and comforted and rewarded them.
translations.idiomatic: Kangsheng assembled the city's elders, proclaimed the imperial edict, and distributed rewards to reassure them.

sentences.zh: 魏以植為兗州刺史，李元護為齊州刺史，席法友為豫州刺史，軍主京兆王世弼為南徐州刺史。

translations.literal: Wei made Zhi Inspector of Yan Province, Li Yuanhu Inspector of Qi Province, Xi Fayou Inspector of Yu Province, and Army Commander Wang Shibi of Jingzhao Inspector of South Xu Province.
translations.idiomatic: Wei appointed Zhi inspector of Yan Province, Li Yuanhu inspector of Qi Province, Xi Fayou inspector of Yu Province, and the army commander Wang Shibi of Jingzhao inspector of South Xu Province.

sentences.zh: 巴西民雍道晞聚眾萬餘逼郡城，巴西太守魯休烈嬰城自守。

translations.literal: The people of Baxi, Yong Daoxi, gathered a crowd of more than ten thousand and pressed the commandery city; the Administrator of Baxi, Lu Xiulie, closed the city and held it himself.
translations.idiomatic: Yong Daoxi of Baxi raised a force of more than ten thousand men and besieged the commandery seat; Lu Xiulie, the administrator of Baxi, shut the gates and held the city.

sentences.zh: 三月，劉季連遣中兵參軍李奉伯帥眾五千救之，與郡兵合擊道晞，斬之。

translations.literal: In the third month, Liu Jilian sent Central Army Major Li Fengbo to command five thousand men to rescue them; together with the commandery troops they struck Daoxi and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, Liu Jilian sent Li Fengbo, a central army major, with five thousand men to relieve the city; together with the commandery troops they attacked Daoxi and killed him.

sentences.zh: 奉伯欲進討郡東餘賊，涪令李膺止之曰：「卒惰將驕，乘勝履險，非完策也；

translations.literal: Fengbo wished to advance and campaign against the remaining bandits east of the commandery; the magistrate of Fu, Li Ying, stopped him, saying: "The soldiers are slack and the general arrogant; riding victory into danger is not a complete strategy;
translations.idiomatic: Fengbo wanted to pursue the remaining rebels east of the commandery, but Li Ying, magistrate of Fu, dissuaded him: "The men are slack and the commander overconfident; pressing a victory into rough country is no sound plan;

sentences.zh: 不如少緩，更思後計。」

translations.literal: it would be better to slacken a little and think again of a later plan."
translations.idiomatic: better pause and think of a follow-up move."

sentences.zh: 奉伯不從，悉眾入山，大敗而還。

translations.literal: Fengbo did not follow; he led all his forces into the mountains and returned after a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Fengbo refused, led his entire force into the hills, and returned in defeat.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，遣平西將軍崔慧景將水軍討壽陽，帝屏除，出琅邪城送之。

translations.literal: On yimao, the General Who Pacifies the West Cui Huijing was sent to lead the water army to campaign against Shouyang; the emperor cleared the screen and went out of Langye city to see him off.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao, Cui Huijing, general who pacifies the west, was dispatched with the fleet to attack Shouyang; the emperor dismissed his attendants and went out through Langye city to see him off.

sentences.zh: 帝戎服坐樓上，召慧景單騎進圍內，無一人自隨者。

translations.literal: The emperor in military dress sat on a tower, summoned Huijing to enter the encirclement alone on horseback, and not a single man accompanied him of his own accord.
translations.idiomatic: Dressed for war, the emperor sat on a tower and called Huijing to ride in alone through the cordon; not one of his men went with him.

sentences.zh: 裁交數言，拜辭而去。

translations.literal: They barely exchanged a few words; he bowed in farewell and departed.
translations.idiomatic: They exchanged only a few words before Huijing bowed and left.

sentences.zh: 慧景既得出，甚喜。

translations.literal: Once Huijing had gotten out, he was very pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Once Huijing was outside the cordon, he was greatly relieved.

sentences.zh: 豫州刺史蕭懿將步軍三萬屯小峴，交州刺史李叔獻屯合肥。

translations.literal: Inspector of Yu Province Xiao Yi led thirty thousand foot soldiers and encamped at Xiaoxian; Inspector of Jiao Province Li Shuxian encamped at Hefei.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yi, inspector of Yu Province, encamped at Xiaoxian with thirty thousand infantry; Li Shuxian, inspector of Jiao Province, held Hefei.

sentences.zh: 懿遣裨將胡松、李導士帥眾萬餘屯死虎。

translations.literal: Yi sent subordinate generals Hu Song and Li Daoshi to command more than ten thousand men and encamp at Sihu.
translations.idiomatic: Yi sent his lieutenants Hu Song and Li Daoshi with more than ten thousand men to camp at Sihu.

sentences.zh: 驃騎司馬陳伯之將水軍溯淮而上，以逼壽陽，軍於硤石。

translations.literal: Marshal of Agile Cavalry Chen Bozhi led the water army up the Huai to press Shouyang and encamped at Xiashi.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Bozhi, marshal of agile cavalry, led the fleet up the Huai to threaten Shouyang and encamped at Xiashi.

sentences.zh: 壽陽士民多謀應齊者。

translations.literal: Many gentry and commoners of Shouyang plotted to respond to Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Many in Shouyang were plotting to side with Qi.

sentences.zh: 魏奚康生降御內外，閉城一月，援軍乃至。

translations.literal: Xi Kangsheng of Wei took command inside and outside, closed the city for one month, and only then did relief troops arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Kangsheng of Wei took control inside and outside the city, kept the gates shut for a month, and only then did reinforcements arrive.

sentences.zh: 丙申，彭城王勰、王肅擊松、伯之等，大破之，進攻合肥，生擒叔獻。

translations.literal: On bingshen, Prince Xie of Pengcheng and Wang Su struck Song, Bozhi, and the others, routed them utterly, advanced to attack Hefei, and captured Shuxian alive.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen, Prince Xie of Pengcheng and Wang Su routed Hu Song, Chen Bozhi, and their forces, then advanced on Hefei and took Li Shuxian alive.

sentences.zh: 統軍宇文福言於勰曰：「建安，淮南重鎮，彼此要衝，得之，則義陽易圖；

translations.literal: Commander-in-Chief Yuwen Fu said to Xie: "Jian'an is a key town of Huainan, a strategic pass for both sides; if we obtain it, then Yiyang is easy to take;
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Fu, commander-in-chief, told Xie: "Jian'an is a vital Huainan stronghold and a crossroads for both sides. Take it, and Yiyang will be easy;

sentences.zh: 不得，則壽陽難保。」

translations.literal: if we do not obtain it, then Shouyang will be hard to preserve."
translations.idiomatic: fail, and Shouyang itself will be hard to hold."

sentences.zh: 勰然之，使福攻建安，建安戍主胡景略面縛出降。

translations.literal: Xie approved; he sent Fu to attack Jian'an, and the garrison commander of Jian'an, Hu Jinglue, came out bound in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Xie agreed and sent Fu against Jian'an; Hu Jinglue, the garrison commander, came out with his hands bound and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 己亥，魏皇弟恌卒。

translations.literal: On jihai, the younger imperial brother of Wei, Ti, died.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai, Ti, a younger brother of the Wei emperor, died.

sentences.zh: 崔慧景之發建康也，其子覺為直閣將軍，密與之約，慧景至廣陵，覺走從之。

translations.literal: When Cui Huijing set out from Jiankang, his son Jue was a direct-attendant general; they had a secret agreement, and when Huijing reached Guangling, Jue fled to follow him.
translations.idiomatic: When Cui Huijing left Jiankang, his son Jue, a direct-attendant general, had made a secret pact with him; when Huijing reached Guangling, Jue deserted and joined him.

sentences.zh: 慧景過廣陵數十里，召會諸軍主曰：「吾荷三帝厚恩，當顧托之重。

translations.literal: Huijing passed Guangling by several tens of li, summoned and met the various army commanders, and said: "I have borne the thick grace of three emperors and the weight of their dying charge.
translations.idiomatic: A few dozen li past Guangling, Huijing called his commanders together and said: "I owe a great debt to three emperors and the trust they placed in me.

sentences.zh: 幼主昏狂，朝廷壞亂；

translations.literal: The young ruler is muddled and mad, and the court is ruined and chaotic;
translations.idiomatic: The young ruler is deranged, and the court is in ruins;

sentences.zh: 危而不扶，責在今日。

translations.literal: to see danger and not support—today the responsibility lies.
translations.idiomatic: who does not steady the state when it totters bears the blame today.

sentences.zh: 欲與諸君共建大功以安社稷，何如？」

translations.literal: I wish to join with you gentlemen in jointly establishing a great achievement to settle the altars of state—what do you say?"
translations.idiomatic: I mean to join you in a great deed to save the realm. Will you follow me?"

sentences.zh: 眾皆響應，於是還軍向廣陵。

translations.literal: The crowd all responded; thereupon he turned the army back toward Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: All assented, and he turned the army back toward Guangling.

sentences.zh: 司馬崔恭祖守廣陵城，開門納之。

translations.literal: Marshal Cui Gongzu guarded Guangling city and opened the gates to admit him.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Gongzu, the marshal, held Guangling and opened the gates to him.

sentences.zh: 帝聞變，壬子，假右衛將軍左興盛節，督建康水陸諸軍以討之。

translations.literal: The emperor heard of the change; on renzi he lent the tally to Right Guard General Zuo Xingsheng and ordered him to command all Jiankang water and land forces to campaign against him.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard of the revolt, on renzi he gave Zuo Xingsheng of the right guard the staff of authority and ordered him to command all land and naval forces in Jiankang against Huijing.

sentences.zh: 慧景停廣陵二日，即收眾濟江。

translations.literal: Huijing halted at Guangling two days, then gathered his forces and crossed the river.
translations.idiomatic: Huijing lingered at Guangling only two days, then gathered his troops and crossed the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 初，南徐、兗二州刺史江夏王寶玄娶徐孝嗣女為妃，孝嗣誅，詔令離婚，寶玄恨望。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Inspector of the two provinces of South Xu and Yan, Prince Bao Xuan of Jiangxia, had married the daughter of Xu Xiaosi as consort; when Xiaosi was executed, an edict ordered divorce, and Bao Xuan harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Prince Bao Xuan of Jiangxia, who held the two provinces of South Xu and Yan, had married Xu Xiaosi's daughter. After Xiaosi was executed, the court ordered the marriage dissolved, and Bao Xuan nursed a bitter grudge.

sentences.zh: 慧景遣使奉寶玄為主，寶玄斬其使，因發將吏守城，帝遣馬軍主戚平、外監黃林夫助鎮京口。

translations.literal: Huijing sent envoys to set up Bao Xuan as leader; Bao Xuan beheaded the envoys, then mobilized officers and clerks to guard the city; the emperor sent Horse Army Commander Qi Ping and Outer Supervisor Huang Linfu to help garrison Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: Huijing sent envoys offering to make Bao Xuan their leader; Bao Xuan beheaded them, mustered his officers to hold the city, and the emperor sent Qi Ping of the horse guard and Huang Linfu, an outer supervisor, to reinforce Jingkou.

sentences.zh: 慧景將渡江，寶玄密與相應，殺司馬孔矜、典簽呂承緒及平、林夫，開門納慧景，使長史沈佚之、咨議柳□分部軍眾。

translations.literal: As Huijing was about to cross the river, Bao Xuan secretly responded in concert, killed Marshal Kong Jin, Registrar Lu Chengxu, and Ping and Linfu, opened the gates to admit Huijing, and had Chief Clerk Shen Yizhi and Adviser Liu Yong divide and deploy the army.
translations.idiomatic: As Huijing prepared to cross the river, Bao Xuan secretly colluded with him, killed the marshal Kong Jin, the registrar Lu Chengxu, and Qi Ping and Huang Linfu, opened the gates to admit Huijing, and had his chief clerk Shen Yizhi and adviser Liu Yong deploy the troops.

sentences.zh: 寶玄乘八□輿，手執絳麾，隨慧景向建康。

translations.literal: Bao Xuan rode an eight-pole sedan, held a crimson banner in hand, and followed Huijing toward Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Xuan rode in an eight-pole sedan, crimson banner in hand, and marched with Huijing on Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 台遣驍騎將軍張佛護、直閣將軍徐元稱等六將據竹裡，為數城以拒之。

translations.literal: The court sent General of Agile Cavalry Zhang Fuhu, Direct-Attendant General Xu Yuancheng, and five other generals to hold Zhuli, building several forts to resist them.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent six generals, including Zhang Fuhu of the agile cavalry and Xu Yuancheng of the direct attendants, to hold Zhuli and build a chain of forts to block them.

sentences.zh: 寶玄遣信謂佛護曰：「身自還朝，君何意苦相斷遏？」

translations.literal: Bao Xuan sent a message to Fuhu, saying: "I myself am returning to court—why do you insist on cutting me off so bitterly?"
translations.idiomatic: Bao Xuan sent word to Fuhu: "I am returning to court of my own accord—why do you block my path so stubbornly?

sentences.zh: 佛護對曰：「小人荷國重恩，使於此創立小戍。

translations.literal: Fuhu replied: "This petty man has borne the state's heavy grace and was sent here to establish a small garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Fuhu replied: "I owe the state a heavy debt and was sent here to hold this little post.

sentences.zh: 殿下還朝，但自直過，豈敢斷遏！」

translations.literal: When Your Highness returns to court, simply pass straight through—how would I dare to cut you off!"
translations.idiomatic: When Your Highness returns to court, pass straight through—how would I dare stop you!

sentences.zh: 遂射慧景軍，因合戰。

translations.literal: He thereupon shot at Huijing's army, and battle joined.
translations.idiomatic: With that he loosed arrows at Huijing's troops, and battle was joined.

sentences.zh: 崔覺、崔恭祖將前鋒，皆荒傖善戰，又輕行不蒸食，以數舫緣江載酒貪為軍糧，每見台軍城中煙火起，輒盡力攻之。

translations.literal: Cui Jue and Cui Gongzu led the vanguard; all were wild northern warriors skilled in battle, and again traveled light without cooking food, using several boats along the river to carry wine and provisions as army grain; whenever they saw court troops' fires rise in a city, they at once attacked with full force.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Jue and Cui Gongzu led the van—hardy frontier fighters who marched light without cooking, loaded several boats along the river with food and wine as their rations, and whenever they saw smoke rise from a garrison town, threw their full weight against it.

sentences.zh: 台軍不復得食，以此饑困。

translations.literal: The court troops could no longer obtain food; because of this they were hungry and distressed.
translations.idiomatic: The defenders could no longer get food and were worn down by hunger.

sentences.zh: 元稱等議，欲降，佛護不可。

translations.literal: Yuancheng and the others discussed wishing to surrender; Fuhu would not allow it.
translations.idiomatic: Yuancheng and others wanted to surrender, but Fuhu refused.

sentences.zh: 恭祖等進攻城，拔之，斬佛護。

translations.literal: Gongzu and the others advanced to attack the city, took it, and beheaded Fuhu.
translations.idiomatic: Gongzu pressed the assault, took the fort, and beheaded Fuhu.

sentences.zh: 徐元稱降，餘四軍主皆死。

translations.literal: Xu Yuancheng surrendered; the remaining four army commanders all died.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yuancheng surrendered; the other four commanders were killed.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，遣中領軍王瑩都督眾軍，據湖頭築壘，上帶蔣山西巖實甲數萬。

translations.literal: On yimao, Central Army Commander Wang Ying was sent to command all armies, hold Hutou and build ramparts, and above on the western cliffs of Mount Jiang solid armor numbered in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao, Wang Ying of the central army was sent to command the forces, fortify Hutou, and post tens of thousands of armored men along the western cliffs of Mount Jiang.

sentences.zh: 瑩，誕之從曾孫也。

translations.literal: Ying was the great-great-grandson of Dan.
translations.idiomatic: Ying was a great-great-grandson of Xiao Dan.

sentences.zh: 慧景至查硎，竹塘人萬副兒說慧景曰：「今平路皆為台軍所斷，不可議進；

translations.literal: When Huijing reached Chaming, Wan Fuer of Zhutang urged Huijing, saying: "Now the level roads are all cut by court troops; advance cannot be discussed;
translations.idiomatic: At Chaming, Wan Fuer of Zhutang told Huijing: "The level roads are all held by the court—you cannot advance that way;

sentences.zh: 唯宜從蔣山龍尾上，出其不意耳。」

translations.literal: you should only go up Mount Jiang by Dragon Tail and take them unawares."
translations.idiomatic: you should climb Mount Jiang by the Dragon Tail path and strike where they do not expect you."

sentences.zh: 慧景從之，分遣千餘人，魚貫緣山自西巖夜下，鼓叫臨城中。

translations.literal: Huijing followed this; he divided and sent more than a thousand men to file like fish along the mountain from the western cliffs by night, beating drums and shouting as they overlooked the city.
translations.idiomatic: Huijing agreed, sent more than a thousand men in single file down the western cliffs by night, and with drums and shouts bore down on the city.

sentences.zh: 台軍驚恐，即時奔散。

translations.literal: The court troops were startled and afraid and at once fled and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: The defenders panicked and fled at once.

sentences.zh: 帝又遣右衛將軍左興盛帥台內三萬人拒慧景於北籬門，興盛望風退走。

translations.literal: The emperor again sent Right Guard General Zuo Xingsheng to command thirty thousand men inside the court to resist Huijing at the North Hedge Gate; Xingsheng saw the wind and retreated in flight.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again sent Zuo Xingsheng of the right guard with thirty thousand palace troops to hold the North Hedge Gate; Xingsheng fled at the first sight of the enemy.

sentences.zh: 甲子，慧景入樂游苑，崔恭祖帥輕騎十餘突入北掖門，乃復出。

translations.literal: On jiazi, Huijing entered the Leyou Park; Cui Gongzu led more than ten light horsemen to burst into the North Flank Gate, then came out again.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi, Huijing entered the Leyou Park; Cui Gongzu led a dozen light horsemen in a dash through the North Flank Gate and out again.

sentences.zh: 宮門皆閉，慧景引眾圍之。

translations.literal: The palace gates were all closed; Huijing led the crowd to besiege them.
translations.idiomatic: The palace gates were shut; Huijing surrounded them with his force.

sentences.zh: 於是東府、石頭、白下、新亭諸城皆潰。

translations.literal: Thereupon the cities of the Eastern Office, Shitou, Baixia, Xinting, and the rest all collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Office, Shitou, Baixia, Xinting, and the other outworks all fell.

sentences.zh: 左興盛走，不得入宮，逃淮渚荻舫中，慧景擒殺之。

translations.literal: Zuo Xingsheng fled, could not enter the palace, escaped into a reed boat on the Huai shallows, and Huijing seized and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo Xingsheng fled, could not re-enter the palace, hid in a reed boat on the riverbank, and was captured and killed by Huijing.

sentences.zh: 宮中遣兵出蕩，不克。

translations.literal: The palace sent troops out to sweep them, but could not overcome them.
translations.idiomatic: Troops sent out from the palace to drive them off failed.

sentences.zh: 慧景燒蘭台府署為戰場。

translations.literal: Huijing burned the Orchid Terrace offices as a battlefield.
translations.idiomatic: Huijing burned the Orchid Terrace offices to clear a battlefield.

sentences.zh: 守衛尉蕭暢屯南掖門，處分城內，隨方應拒，眾心稍安。

translations.literal: Guard Commandant Xiao Chang encamped at the South Flank Gate, disposed affairs within the city, and responded in each quarter as needed; the hearts of the crowd grew somewhat settled.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Chang of the Guard Command encamped at the South Flank Gate, organized the city's defense, and met each threat as it arose, which steadied public morale.

sentences.zh: 慧景稱宣德太后令，廢帝為吳王。

translations.literal: Huijing proclaimed an order of Empress Dowager Xuande and deposed the emperor as Prince of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Huijing proclaimed an edict in the name of Empress Dowager Xuande deposing the emperor as prince of Wu.

sentences.zh: 陳顯達之反也，帝復召諸王侯入宮。

translations.literal: When Chen Xianda rebelled, the emperor again summoned the various princes and marquises into the palace.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Xianda rebelled, the emperor again summoned the princes and marquises into the palace.

sentences.zh: 巴陵王昭冑懲永泰之難，與弟永新侯昭穎詐為沙門，逃於江西。

translations.literal: Prince Zhao Zhou of Baling, taking warning from the calamity of Yongtai, with his younger brother Marquis Zhao Ying of Yongxin feigned being monks and fled to the lands west of the river.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Zhao Zhou of Baling, mindful of the Yongtai massacre, and his brother Marquis Zhao Ying of Yongxin disguised themselves as monks and fled west of the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 昭冑，子良之子也。

translations.literal: Zhao Zhou was the son of Ziliang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Zhou was a son of Xiao Ziliang.

sentences.zh: 及慧景舉兵，昭冑兄弟出赴之。

translations.literal: When Huijing raised troops, the Zhao Zhou brothers went out to join him.
translations.idiomatic: When Huijing took up arms, the brothers came out to join him.

sentences.zh: 慧景意更向昭冑，猶豫未知所立。

translations.literal: Huijing's intent turned more toward Zhao Zhou; he hesitated, not knowing whom to establish.
translations.idiomatic: Huijing's thoughts turned toward making Zhao Zhou ruler, but he hesitated, unable to decide whom to enthrone.

sentences.zh: 竹裡之捷，崔覺與崔恭祖爭功，慧景不能決。

translations.literal: After the victory at Zhuli, Cui Jue and Cui Gongzu contended for merit; Huijing could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: After the victory at Zhuli, Cui Jue and Cui Gongzu quarreled over credit, and Huijing could not settle the dispute.

sentences.zh: 恭祖勸慧景以火箭燒北掖樓。

translations.literal: Gongzu urged Huijing to use fire arrows to burn the North Flank Tower.
translations.idiomatic: Gongzu urged Huijing to burn the North Flank Tower with fire arrows.

sentences.zh: 慧景以大事垂定，後若更造，費用功多，不從。

translations.literal: Huijing considered that the great affair was nearly settled and that if later they had to rebuild, the cost in labor would be great; he did not follow this.
translations.idiomatic: Huijing thought the outcome was all but decided and that rebuilding afterward would cost too much labor, and refused.

sentences.zh: 慧景性好談義，兼解佛理，頓法輪寺，對客高談，恭祖深懷怨望。

translations.literal: Huijing by nature loved discoursing on principles and also understood Buddhist doctrine; he halted at Falun Temple and held lofty discourse with guests; Gongzu harbored deep resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Huijing loved learned debate and knew Buddhist doctrine; he paused at Falun Temple to hold forth with visitors while Gongzu seethed with resentment.

sentences.zh: 時豫州刺史蕭懿將兵在小峴，帝遣密使告之。

translations.literal: At that time Inspector of Yu Province Xiao Yi was leading troops at Xiaoxian; the emperor sent a secret messenger to inform him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yi, inspector of Yu Province, was encamped at Xiaoxian with his army; the emperor sent him word in secret.

sentences.zh: 懿方食，投箸而起，帥軍主胡松、李居士等數千人自採石濟江，頓越城舉火，城中鼓叫稱慶。

translations.literal: Yi was just eating; he cast down his chopsticks and rose, led Army Commanders Hu Song, Li Jushi, and several thousand men to cross the river from Caishi, encamped at Yuecheng and raised fires, and within the city drums sounded and shouts of celebration rang.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was at his meal; he dropped his chopsticks, sprang up, and with Hu Song, Li Jushi, and several thousand men crossed from Caishi, encamped at Yuecheng, and lit signal fires while the city erupted in drums and cheers.

sentences.zh: 恭祖先勸慧景遣二千人斷西岸兵，令不得渡。

translations.literal: Gongzu had earlier urged Huijing to send two thousand men to cut off the troops on the west bank and keep them from crossing.
translations.idiomatic: Gongzu had earlier urged Huijing to post two thousand men to block the western shore and prevent a crossing.

sentences.zh: 慧景以城旦夕降，外救自然應散，不從。

translations.literal: Huijing considered that the city would surrender within days and outside relief would naturally scatter; he did not follow this.
translations.idiomatic: Huijing believed the city would fall within days and outside relief would melt away on its own, and refused.

sentences.zh: 至是，恭祖請擊懿軍，又不許；

translations.literal: At this point Gongzu requested to strike Yi's army, and again it was not permitted;
translations.idiomatic: Now Gongzu asked to attack Yi's force, and again was refused;

sentences.zh: 獨遣崔覺將精手數千人渡南岸。

translations.literal: he sent only Cui Jue to lead several thousand picked men to cross to the south bank.
translations.idiomatic: Huijing sent only Cui Jue with several thousand picked men across to the south bank.

sentences.zh: 懿軍昧旦進戰，數合，士皆致死，覺大敗，赴淮死者二千餘人。

translations.literal: Yi's army advanced to battle at dawn; after several engagements the soldiers all fought to the death; Jue was utterly defeated, and more than two thousand who rushed into the Huai died.
translations.idiomatic: Yi's men attacked at dawn; after several clashes their troops fought to the death; Jue was routed, and more than two thousand drowned in the Huai.

sentences.zh: 覺單馬退，開桁阻淮。

translations.literal: Jue retreated alone on horseback and opened the pontoon bridge to block the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Jue fled alone on horseback and raised the pontoon bridge to block pursuit across the Huai.

sentences.zh: 恭祖掠得東宮女伎，覺逼奪之。

translations.literal: Gongzu had plundered female performers of the Eastern Palace; Jue forced and seized them from him.
translations.idiomatic: Gongzu had seized palace entertainers from the Eastern Palace; Jue forced him to give them up.

sentences.zh: 恭祖積忿恨，其夜，與慧景驍將劉靈運詣城降，眾心離壞。

translations.literal: Gongzu accumulated resentment and hatred; that night, with Huijing's fierce general Liu Lingyun, he went to the city to surrender, and the hearts of the crowd split and collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Gongzu's fury boiled over; that night he and Huijing's fierce general Liu Lingyun went to the city and surrendered, and the army's morale collapsed.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，癸酉，慧景將腹心數人潛去，欲北渡江；

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on guiyou, Huijing led several trusted men in secret departure, wishing to cross the river north;
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on guiyou, Huijing slipped away with a few confidants, intending to flee north across the river;

sentences.zh: 城北諸軍不知，猶為拒戰。

translations.literal: the armies north of the city did not know and still fought in resistance.
translations.idiomatic: the troops north of the city, unaware, still fought on.

sentences.zh: 城中出蕩，殺數百人。

translations.literal: Troops came out from the city to sweep them and killed several hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: Defenders sallied forth and killed several hundred of them.

sentences.zh: 懿軍渡北岸，慧景餘眾皆走。

translations.literal: Yi's army crossed to the north bank; Huijing's remaining crowd all fled.
translations.idiomatic: Yi's force crossed to the north bank, and Huijing's remaining troops scattered.

sentences.zh: 慧景圍城凡十二日而敗，從者於道稍散，單騎至蟹浦，為漁人所斬，以頭內鰍籃，擔送建康。

translations.literal: Huijing besieged the city for twelve days in all and then was defeated; followers on the road gradually scattered; he rode alone to Xiepu and was beheaded by a fisherman, his head placed in a minnow basket and carried to Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: Huijing had besieged the city twelve days before he was broken; his followers melted away along the road; he rode alone to Xiepu, where a fisherman cut off his head, packed it in a fish basket, and carried it to Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 恭祖系尚方，少時殺之。

translations.literal: Gongzu was bound in the Imperial Workshops; after a short time he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Gongzu was imprisoned in the Imperial Workshops and soon executed.

sentences.zh: 覺亡命為道人，捕獲，伏誅。

translations.literal: Jue fled his life and became a Daoist priest; he was captured and executed.
translations.idiomatic: Jue fled and became a Daoist priest; he was captured and put to death.

sentences.zh: 寶玄初至建康，軍於東城，士民多往投集。

translations.literal: When Bao Xuan first reached Jiankang, he encamped at the eastern city; gentry and commoners mostly went to join and gather.
translations.idiomatic: When Bao Xuan first reached Jiankang, he camped east of the city, and many townspeople flocked to him.

sentences.zh: 慧景敗，收得朝野投寶玄及慧景人名，帝令燒之，曰：「江夏尚爾，豈可復罪餘人！」

translations.literal: When Huijing was defeated, they collected the names of court and countryside who had joined Bao Xuan and Huijing; the emperor ordered them burned, saying: "Jiangxia is still like this—how could we again punish the rest!"
translations.idiomatic: After Huijing's defeat, the court gathered lists of those who had sided with Bao Xuan and Huijing; the emperor ordered them burned, saying: "If even Jiangxia is treated so, how can we punish everyone else!

sentences.zh: 寶玄逃亡數日，乃出。

translations.literal: Bao Xuan fled several days, then came out.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Xuan hid several days, then gave himself up.

sentences.zh: 帝召入後堂，以步障裹之，令左右數十人鳴鼓角馳繞其外，遣人謂寶玄曰：「汝近圍我亦如此耳。」

translations.literal: The emperor summoned him into the rear hall, wrapped him in a screen of cloth, ordered several tens of attendants to beat drums and horns and gallop circling outside, and sent someone to tell Bao Xuan: "When you lately besieged me, it was also like this."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned him to the rear hall, wrapped him in cloth screens, had dozens of attendants beat drums and horns and ride circles around him, and sent word: "When you besieged me, it was just like this."

sentences.zh: 初，慧景欲交處士何點，點不顧。

translations.literal: Earlier, Huijing wished to befriend the recluse He Dian; Dian paid no attention.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Huijing had sought the friendship of the recluse He Dian, who ignored him.

sentences.zh: 及圍建康，逼召點。

translations.literal: When he besieged Jiankang, he forced Dian to be summoned.
translations.idiomatic: When he besieged Jiankang, he compelled Dian to come.

sentences.zh: 點往赴其軍，終日談義，不及軍事。

translations.literal: Dian went to join his army and all day discoursed on principles, not touching military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Dian went to his camp and spent the whole day in learned talk, never mentioning the war.

sentences.zh: 慧景敗，帝欲殺點。

translations.literal: When Huijing was defeated, the emperor wished to kill Dian.
translations.idiomatic: After Huijing's defeat, the emperor wanted He Dian executed.

sentences.zh: 蕭暢謂茹法珍曰：「點若不誘賊共講，未易可量。

translations.literal: Xiao Chang said to Ru Fazhen: "If Dian had not lured the rebels to discourse together, he would not be easy to measure.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Chang told Ru Fazhen: "If Dian had not kept the rebels talking all day, who knows what might have happened.

sentences.zh: 以此言之，乃應得封！」

translations.literal: Speaking from this, he ought to receive enfeoffment!"
translations.idiomatic: By that reckoning, he deserves a noble title!"

sentences.zh: 帝乃止。

translations.literal: The emperor then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor relented.

sentences.zh: 點，胤之兄也。

translations.literal: Dian was the elder brother of Yin.
translations.idiomatic: Dian was the elder brother of He Yin.

sentences.zh: 蕭懿既去小峴，王肅亦還洛陽。

translations.literal: Once Xiao Yi had left Xiaoxian, Wang Su also returned to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: After Xiao Yi left Xiaoxian, Wang Su also returned to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 荒人往來者妄雲肅復謀歸國；

translations.literal: Frontier people coming and going falsely said Su again plotted to return to his state;
translations.idiomatic: Frontier travelers spread false word that Su was plotting to return to Qi;

sentences.zh: 五月，乙巳，詔以肅為都督豫、徐、司三州諸軍事、豫州刺史、西豐公。

translations.literal: in the fifth month, on yisi, an edict made Su Commander of all military affairs in Yu, Xu, and Si provinces, Inspector of Yu Province, and Duke of Xifeng.
translations.idiomatic: in the fifth month, on yisi, the court appointed Su commander of military affairs in Yu, Xu, and Si provinces, inspector of Yu Province, and duke of Xifeng.

sentences.zh: 己酉，江夏王寶玄伏誅。

translations.literal: On jiyou, Prince Bao Xuan of Jiangxia was executed.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou, Prince Bao Xuan of Jiangxia was executed.

sentences.zh: 壬子，大赦。

translations.literal: On renzi, a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi, the court proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 六月，丙子，魏彭城王勰進位大司馬，領司徒；

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on bingzi, Prince Xie of Pengcheng of Wei advanced in rank to Grand Marshal and concurrently held the post of Minister of Works;
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on bingzi, Prince Xie of Pengcheng of Wei was promoted to grand marshal and retained the post of minister of works;

sentences.zh: 王肅加開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: Wang Su was given the additional title of Grand Master with golden seal and purple ribbon of the third rank.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Su was given the additional title of grand master with golden seal and purple ribbon of the third rank.

sentences.zh: 太陽蠻田育丘等二萬八千戶附於魏，魏置四郡十八縣。

translations.literal: The Taiyang barbarians, Tian Yuqiu and others, twenty-eight thousand households submitted to Wei; Wei established four commanderies and eighteen counties.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Yuqiu of the Taiyang barbarians and others, twenty-eight thousand households in all, submitted to Wei, which established four commanderies and eighteen counties for them.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，曲赦建康、南徐、兗二州。

translations.literal: On yichou, a partial amnesty was granted to Jiankang and the two provinces of South Xu and Yan.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou, a partial amnesty was granted to Jiankang and the two provinces of South Xu and Yan.

sentences.zh: 先是，崔慧景既平，詔赦其黨。

translations.literal: Earlier, once Cui Huijing had been pacified, an edict amnestied his faction.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after Cui Huijing's revolt was crushed, an edict had amnestied his followers.

sentences.zh: 而嬖倖用事，不依詔書，無罪而家富者，皆誣為賊黨，殺而籍其貲；

translations.literal: But the favorites held power and did not follow the edict; those without guilt but with wealthy families were all falsely accused as rebel partisans, killed, and their property registered and seized;
translations.idiomatic: But the emperor's favorites ignored the edict: innocent but wealthy families were branded rebels, killed, and their property seized;

sentences.zh: 實附賊而盆者皆不問。

translations.literal: those who truly joined the rebels but were poor were all left uninvestigated.
translations.idiomatic: those who had actually joined the rebels but were poor went unpunished.

sentences.zh: 或謂中書舍人王咺之云：「赦書無信，人情大惡。」

translations.literal: Someone said to Secretariat Attendant Wang Yanzhi: "The amnesty document has no credibility; popular feeling is greatly bitter."
translations.idiomatic: Someone told Wang Yanzhi of the Secretariat: "The amnesty means nothing; the people are furious."

sentences.zh: 咺之曰：「正當復有赦耳。」

translations.literal: Yanzhi said: "There will simply be another amnesty."
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhi replied: "There will simply be another amnesty."

sentences.zh: 由是再赦。

translations.literal: Because of this there was a second amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: So they proclaimed a second amnesty.

sentences.zh: 既而嬖倖誅縱亦如初。

translations.literal: Soon after, the favorites' executions and license were again as before.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the favorites were killing and plundering as before.

sentences.zh: 是時，帝所寵左右凡三十一人，黃門十人。

translations.literal: At this time, those the emperor favored at his side numbered thirty-one in all, and ten yellow-gate attendants.
translations.idiomatic: At this time the emperor kept thirty-one favorites at his side, including ten yellow-gate attendants.

sentences.zh: 直閣、驍騎將軍徐世心剽素為帝所委任，凡有殺戮，皆在其手。

translations.literal: Direct-Attendant and General of Agile Cavalry Xu Shixinpiao had long been entrusted by the emperor; whenever there were killings, all were in his hands.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Shixinpiao, a direct-attendant general of agile cavalry, had long been the emperor's chosen executioner; killings were his work.

sentences.zh: 及陳顯達事起，加輔國將軍；

translations.literal: When Chen Xianda's affair arose, he was given the additional post of General Who Assists the State;
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Xianda rebelled, he was made general who assists the state;

sentences.zh: 雖用護軍崔慧景為都督，而兵權實在世心剽。

translations.literal: although Guardian of the Army Cui Huijing was used as commander, in fact military authority lay with Shixinpiao.
translations.idiomatic: though Cui Huijing of the guard was named commander, real military power rested with Shixinpiao.

sentences.zh: 世心剽亦知帝昏縱，密謂其黨茹法珍、梅蟲兒曰：「何世天子無要人，但儂貨主惡耳！」

translations.literal: Shixinpiao also knew the emperor was muddled and dissolute; he secretly told his faction Ru Fazhen and Mei Chong'er: "What age lacks a ruler's essential men—it is only that our master is vile!"
translations.idiomatic: Shixinpiao knew the emperor was deranged and told his allies Ru Fazhen and Mei Chong'er in secret: "Every age has its indispensable men—only our master is worthless!

sentences.zh: 法珍等與之爭權，以白帝。

translations.literal: Fazhen and the others contended for power with him and reported to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Fazhen and the others fought him for power and denounced him to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝稍惡其凶強，遣禁兵殺之，世心剽拒戰而死。

translations.literal: The emperor gradually hated his fierceness and strength, sent palace guards to kill him, and Shixinpiao resisted in battle and died.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor came to hate his brutality and sent palace guards to kill him; Shixinpiao fought back and died.

sentences.zh: 自是法珍、蟲兒用事，並為外監，口稱詔敕；

translations.literal: From this Fazhen and Chong'er held power, both became outer supervisors, and with their mouths proclaimed edicts;
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter Fazhen and Chong'er ruled as outer supervisors, issuing orders in the emperor's name;

sentences.zh: 王咺之專掌文翰，與相脣齒。

translations.literal: Wang Yanzhi alone managed documents and correspondence, and with them was lip to teeth.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yanzhi controlled the paperwork, and the three ruled as one.

sentences.zh: 帝呼所幸潘貴妃父寶慶及茹法珍為阿丈，梅蟲兒及俞靈韻為阿兄。

translations.literal: The emperor called the father of his beloved Consort Pan, Baoqing, and Ru Fazhen "Uncle"; Mei Chong'er and Yu Lingyun he called "Elder Brother."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor called Consort Pan's father Baoqing and Ru Fazhen "Uncle," and Mei Chong'er and Yu Lingyun "Elder Brother."

sentences.zh: 帝與法珍等俱詣寶慶家，躬身汲水，助豆人作膳。

translations.literal: The emperor with Fazhen and the others all went to Baoqing's home, personally drew water, and helped the kitchen servants prepare food.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor visited Baoqing's house with Fazhen and the others, drew water himself, and helped the cooks prepare the meal.

sentences.zh: 寶慶恃勢作奸，富人悉誣以罪，田宅貲財，莫不啟乞。

translations.literal: Baoqing relied on power to commit wrongdoing; the wealthy were all falsely accused of crimes; fields, houses, and property—none were not reported and begged for.
translations.idiomatic: Baoqing abused his power: wealthy families were framed on false charges, and their lands, houses, and goods were all seized on petition.

sentences.zh: 一家被陷，禍及親鄰。

translations.literal: When one family was trapped, disaster reached kin and neighbors.
translations.idiomatic: When one household fell, kin and neighbors were ruined with it.

sentences.zh: 又慮後患，盡殺其男口。

translations.literal: Again fearing later trouble, they killed all the males in those families.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing later reprisals, they killed every male in those families.

sentences.zh: 帝數往諸刀敕家游宴，有吉凶輒往慶吊。

translations.literal: The emperor repeatedly went to the various Dao Jiao households for feasting and play; whenever there was fortune or misfortune he at once went to congratulate or mourn.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor often visited the households of his sword-guard favorites for feasts, and attended their weddings and funerals.

sentences.zh: 奄人王寶孫，年十三四，號「倀子」，最有寵，參預朝政，雖王咺之、梅蟲兒之徒亦下之；

translations.literal: Eunuch Wang Baosun, aged thirteen or fourteen, called "Changzi," was most favored, participated in court governance, and even Wang Yanzhi, Mei Chong'er, and their sort were beneath him;
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Wang Baosun, thirteen or fourteen years old, nicknamed "Changzi," was the favorite of favorites; he took part in government, and even Wang Yanzhi and Mei Chong'er bowed to him;

sentences.zh: 控制大臣，移易詔敕，乃至騎馬入殿，詆訶天子；

translations.literal: he controlled great ministers, altered edicts and orders, and even rode a horse into the hall and reviled the Son of Heaven;
translations.idiomatic: he dominated senior ministers, altered edicts, rode his horse into the audience hall, and berated the emperor;

sentences.zh: 公卿見之，莫不懾息焉。

translations.literal: when the high officials saw him, none did not shrink and hold their breath.
translations.idiomatic: the high officials trembled before him.

sentences.zh: 吐谷渾王伏連籌事魏盡禮，而居其國，置百官，皆如天子之制，稱制於其鄰國。

translations.literal: The king of Tuyuhun, Fulianchou, served Wei with full ritual propriety, yet dwelt in his own state, established the hundred offices, all like the Son of Heaven's system, and proclaimed imperial rule toward neighboring states.
translations.idiomatic: Fulianchou, king of Tuyuhun, observed every courtesy toward Wei while ruling his own realm with a full court like an emperor's and treating neighboring states as his subjects.

sentences.zh: 魏主遣使責而宥之。

translations.literal: The ruler of Wei sent envoys to rebuke him and then pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor sent envoys to rebuke him, then pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 冠軍將軍、驃騎司馬陳伯之再引兵攻壽陽，魏彭城王勰拒之。

translations.literal: Champion General and Marshal of Agile Cavalry Chen Bozhi again led troops to attack Shouyang; Prince Xie of Pengcheng of Wei resisted him.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Bozhi, champion general and marshal of agile cavalry, again attacked Shouyang; Prince Xie of Pengcheng of Wei held the city against him.

sentences.zh: 援軍未至，汝陰太守傅永將郡兵三千救壽陽。

translations.literal: Relief troops had not arrived; the Administrator of Ruyin, Fu Yong, led three thousand commandery troops to rescue Shouyang.
translations.idiomatic: Before relief arrived, Fu Yong, administrator of Ruyin, marched three thousand commandery troops to relieve Shouyang.

sentences.zh: 伯之防淮口甚固，永去淮口二十餘里，牽船上汝水南岸，以水牛挽之，直南趣淮，下船即渡；

translations.literal: Bozhi defended the Huai mouth very firmly; Yong went more than twenty li from the Huai mouth, hauled boats onto the south bank of the Ru River, used water buffalo to drag them, went straight south toward the Huai, and disembarked to cross at once;
translations.idiomatic: Bozhi held the Huai mouth tightly; Yong went more than twenty li upstream, hauled his boats onto the south bank of the Ru, had water buffalo drag them straight south to the Huai, and crossed the moment they reached the water;

sentences.zh: 適上南岸，齊兵亦至。

translations.literal: just as he reached the south bank, Qi troops also arrived.
translations.idiomatic: and as his men landed, Qi troops arrived on the spot.

sentences.zh: 會夜，永潛進入城，勰喜甚，曰：「吾北望已久，恐洛陽難可復見，不意卿能至也。」

translations.literal: It happened to be night; Yong secretly advanced into the city; Xie was very pleased and said: "I have long looked north; I feared Luoyang would be hard to see again—I did not expect you could arrive."
translations.idiomatic: By night Yong stole into the city. Xie was overjoyed and said: "I have watched the north so long, fearing I would never see Luoyang again—I never expected you could come."

sentences.zh: 勰令永引兵入城，永曰：「永之此來，欲以卻敵；

translations.literal: Xie ordered Yong to lead troops into the city; Yong said: "Yong's coming here is to repel the enemy;
translations.idiomatic: Xie ordered Yong to bring his men inside the walls. Yong said: "I came to drive the enemy off;

sentences.zh: 若如教旨，乃是與殿下同受功圍，豈救援之意！」

translations.literal: if I follow the instruction as given, that is to suffer siege together with Your Highness—how is that the intent of rescue!"
translations.idiomatic: if I obey that order, I merely share the siege with Your Highness—that is not rescue!

sentences.zh: 遂軍於城外。

translations.literal: He thereupon encamped outside the city.
translations.idiomatic: He encamped outside the city instead.

sentences.zh: 秋，八月，乙酉，勰部分將士，與永並勢擊伯之於肥口，大破之，斬首九千，俘獲一萬。

translations.literal: In autumn, the eighth month, on yiyou, Xie disposed his officers and soldiers, and with Yong in combined force struck Bozhi at Feikou, routed him utterly, beheaded nine thousand, and captured ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the eighth month, on yiyou, Xie deployed his forces and, joining Fu Yong, routed Chen Bozhi at Feikou, taking nine thousand heads and ten thousand prisoners.

sentences.zh: 伯之脫身遁還，淮南遂入於魏。

translations.literal: Bozhi slipped away and fled back; Huainan thereupon passed into Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Bozhi escaped with his life; Huainan then fell to Wei.

sentences.zh: 魏遣鎮南將軍元英將兵救淮南，未至，伯之已敗，魏主召勰還洛陽。

translations.literal: Wei sent General Who Guards the South Yuan Ying to lead troops to rescue Huainan; before he arrived, Bozhi was already defeated; the ruler of Wei summoned Xie back to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Wei sent Yuan Ying, general who guards the south, to relieve Huainan, but before he arrived Bozhi was already beaten; the Wei emperor recalled Xie to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 勰累表辭大司馬、領司徒，乞還中山；

translations.literal: Xie repeatedly memorialized to decline Grand Marshal and concurrent Minister of Works and begged to return to Zhongshan;
translations.idiomatic: Xie repeatedly asked to resign as grand marshal and minister of works and return to Zhongshan;

sentences.zh: 魏主不許。

translations.literal: the ruler of Wei did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 以元英行揚州事，尋以王肅為都督淮南諸軍事、揚州刺史，持節代之。

translations.literal: Yuan Ying was made to act in Yang Province affairs; soon Wang Su was made Commander of all military affairs in Huainan, Inspector of Yang Province, bearer of the staff to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Ying was put in charge of Yang Province; soon Wang Su was made commander of Huainan military affairs, inspector of Yang Province, and sent with the staff of authority to replace him.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，夜，後宮火。

translations.literal: On jiachen, at night, the rear palace caught fire.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen, at night, fire broke out in the rear palace.

sentences.zh: 時帝出未還，宮內人不得出，外人不敢輒開；

translations.literal: At that time the emperor had gone out and not returned; people inside the palace could not get out, and those outside did not dare open the gates rashly;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was away; those inside could not get out, and those outside dared not open the gates;

sentences.zh: 比及開，死者相枕，燒三千餘間。

translations.literal: by the time they were opened, the dead lay pillow to pillow; more than three thousand rooms were burned.
translations.idiomatic: and by the time the gates were opened, the dead lay in heaps and more than three thousand rooms had burned.

sentences.zh: 時嬖倖之徒皆號為鬼。

translations.literal: At that time the favorites all were called "ghosts."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's favorites were all nicknamed "ghosts."

sentences.zh: 有趙鬼者，能讀《西京賦》，言於帝曰：「柏梁既災，建章是營。」

translations.literal: There was one called Ghost Zhao who could read the "Rhapsody on the Western Capital"; he said to the emperor: "Once Bolang Terrace burned, Jianzhang Palace was built."
translations.idiomatic: One called Ghost Zhao, who could recite the "Rhapsody on the Western Capital," told the emperor: "When Bolang Terrace burned down, they built Jianzhang Palace."

sentences.zh: 帝乃大起芳樂、玉壽等諸殿以麝香塗壁，刻畫裝飾，窮極綺麗。

translations.literal: The emperor then on a great scale raised the various halls such as Fangle and Yushou, smeared the walls with musk, carved and painted ornament, and exhausted the utmost in splendor.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then built Fangle, Yushou, and other halls on a grand scale, coated the walls with musk, carved and painted them, and lavished every luxury upon them.

sentences.zh: 役者自夜達曉，猶不副速。

translations.literal: The laborers from night reached dawn yet still could not keep pace with the speed demanded.
translations.idiomatic: Laborers worked from night till dawn yet still could not keep up with his demands.

sentences.zh: 後宮服御，極選珍奇，府庫舊物，不復周用。

translations.literal: For the rear palace's garments and equipage, the choicest rarities were selected; old items in the treasury were no longer sufficient for use.
translations.idiomatic: The rear palace's wardrobe was stocked with the rarest luxuries; the old stores in the treasury no longer sufficed.

sentences.zh: 貴市民間金寶，價皆數倍。

translations.literal: They prized and bought gold and jewels from among the people; prices all rose several fold.
translations.idiomatic: Gold and jewels were bought up in the markets at several times their normal price.

sentences.zh: 建康酒租皆折使輸金，猶不能足。

translations.literal: Jiankang's wine tax was all converted to require payment in gold, yet still could not suffice.
translations.idiomatic: Even when Jiankang's wine tax was collected entirely in gold, the treasury still could not keep up.

sentences.zh: 鑿金為蓮華以帖地，令潘妃行其上，曰：「此步步生蓮華也。」

translations.literal: They carved gold into lotus flowers to paste on the ground and made Consort Pan walk upon them, saying: "This is lotus flowers born at every step."
translations.idiomatic: Gold was carved into lotus blossoms and laid on the floor for Consort Pan to walk on, and he said, "With every step a lotus blooms."

sentences.zh: 又訂出雉頭、鶴氅、白鷺縗。

translations.literal: They also ordered out pheasant-head garments, crane cloaks, and egret mourning dress.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered extravagant garments of pheasant-head fur, crane-feather cloaks, and egret-plume mourning dress.

sentences.zh: 嬖倖因緣為奸利，課一輸十。

translations.literal: The favorites used opportunities for illicit profit; one assessed unit required ten times the payment.
translations.idiomatic: The favorites used every pretext to extort profit, demanding tenfold what was assessed.

sentences.zh: 又各就州縣求人為輸，准取見直，不為輸送，守宰皆不敢言，重更科斂。

translations.literal: Again each went to the provinces and counties to seek people to make the payments; they approved taking cash on the spot and did not make delivery; the guardians and magistrates all dared not speak, and levied again in layers.
translations.idiomatic: They also sent agents to the provinces and counties to collect from private individuals, took cash on the spot without delivering it to the treasury, and the local officials dared not protest, so the levies were imposed again and again.

sentences.zh: 如此相仍，前後不息。

translations.literal: Thus one after another, front and back without cease.
translations.idiomatic: This went on without pause, one round after another.

sentences.zh: 百姓困盡，號泣道路。

translations.literal: The common people were exhausted to the limit and wailed and wept on the roads.
translations.idiomatic: The people were driven to destitution and wept in the streets.

sentences.zh: 軍主吳子陽等出三關侵魏，九月，與魏東豫州刺史田益宗戰於長風城，子陽等敗還。

translations.literal: Army Commander Wu Ziyang and others went out through the Three Passes to invade Wei; in the ninth month they battled with Wei Eastern Inspector of Yu Province Tian Yizong at Changfeng city; Ziyang and the others were defeated and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Army commander Wu Ziyang and others marched out through the Three Passes to raid Wei; in the ninth month they fought Tian Yizong, Wei's eastern inspector of Yu Province, at Changfeng city, were defeated, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 蕭懿之入援也，蕭衍馳使所親虞安福說懿曰：「誅賊之後，則有不賞之功。

translations.literal: When Xiao Yi entered to give aid, Xiao Yan sent a swift messenger, his close associate Yu Anfu, to persuade Yi, saying: "After executing the rebels, there will then be merit beyond reward.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Yi marched to relieve the capital, Xiao Yan sent his confidant Yu Anfu to urge him: "Once the rebels are destroyed, your merit will be beyond any reward.

sentences.zh: 當明君賢主，尚或難立；

translations.literal: Even with a clear ruler and worthy sovereign, one might still be hard to establish;
translations.idiomatic: Even under a wise ruler it is hard to survive such glory;

sentences.zh: 況於亂朝，何以自免！

translations.literal: how much more in a chaotic court—how could one preserve oneself!
translations.idiomatic: how then in this ruined court can you save yourself!

sentences.zh: 若賊滅之後，仍勒兵入宮，行伊、霍故事，此萬世一時。

translations.literal: If after the rebels are destroyed you still lead troops into the palace and perform the precedent of Yi Yin and Huo Guang, this is a once-in-ten-thousand-generations moment.
translations.idiomatic: If after the rebels are crushed you lead your troops into the palace and play Yi Yin and Huo Guang, you will seize the chance of ages.

sentences.zh: 若不欲爾，便放表還歷陽，托以外拒為事，則威振內外，誰敢不從！

translations.literal: If you do not wish this, then submit a memorial to return to Liyang, using resistance to outside foes as your pretext; then your authority will shake inside and outside—who would dare not follow!
translations.idiomatic: If you will not do that, submit a memorial to return to Liyang on the pretext of guarding against external enemies, and your authority will awe the realm—who would dare disobey!

sentences.zh: 一朝放兵，受其厚爵，高而無民，必生後悔。」

translations.literal: In one morning disband the army and accept their thick rank and salary—lofty yet without the people, you will surely later regret it."
translations.idiomatic: If you disband your army and accept a grand title instead, you will stand high without the people's support and regret it later.

sentences.zh: 長史徐曜甫亦苦勸之，懿並不從。

translations.literal: Chief Clerk Xu Yaofu also urged him bitterly; Yi did not follow any of this.
translations.idiomatic: Chief clerk Xu Yaofu urged him just as strongly; Yi would not listen.

sentences.zh: 崔慧景死，懿為尚書令。

translations.literal: When Cui Huijing died, Yi became Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: After Cui Huijing's death, Yi became director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 有弟九人：敷、衍、暢、融、宏、偉、秀、憺、恢。

translations.literal: He had nine younger brothers: Fu, Yan, Chang, Rong, Hong, Wei, Xiu, Dan, and Hui.
translations.idiomatic: He had nine younger brothers: Fu, Yan, Chang, Rong, Hong, Wei, Xiu, Dan, and Hui.

sentences.zh: 懿以元勳居朝右，暢為衛尉，掌管籥。

translations.literal: Yi by founding merit occupied the right of the court; Chang was Commandant of the Guard and controlled the keys.
translations.idiomatic: As a founding hero Yi stood at the head of the court; Chang was commandant of the guard and held the palace keys.

sentences.zh: 時帝出入無度，或勸懿因其出門，舉兵廢之；

translations.literal: At that time the emperor went in and out without measure; some urged Yi that when he went out the gate, he should raise troops and depose him;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor came and went without restraint; some urged Yi to seize the moment when he left the palace and depose him;

sentences.zh: 懿不聽。

translations.literal: Yi would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Yi refused.

sentences.zh: 嬖臣茹法珍、王咺之等憚懿威權，說帝曰：「懿將行隆昌故事，陛下命在晷刻。」

translations.literal: The favorite ministers Ru Fazhen, Wang Yanzhi, and others feared Yi's authority and power; they told the emperor: "Yi is about to perform the Longchang precedent—Your Majesty's life hangs on the sundial's shadow."
translations.idiomatic: The favorites Ru Fazhen and Wang Yanzhi feared Yi's power and told the emperor: "Yi is about to repeat the Longchang coup—Your Majesty's life is measured in moments."

sentences.zh: 帝然之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 徐曜甫知之，密具舟江渚，勸懿西奔襄陽。

translations.literal: Xu Yaofu learned of it, secretly prepared boats on the river shallows, and urged Yi to flee west to Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yaofu learned of the plot, secretly prepared boats on the riverbank, and urged Yi to flee west to Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 懿曰：「自古皆有死，豈有叛走尚書令邪！」

translations.literal: Yi said: "From antiquity all have death—how could there be a Director of the Masters of Writing who rebels and flees!"
translations.idiomatic: Yi said: "Death comes to everyone—would a director of the Masters of Writing flee like a traitor!

sentences.zh: 懿弟侄鹹為之備。

translations.literal: Yi's younger brothers and nephews all made preparations for him.
translations.idiomatic: His brothers and nephews all made ready to defend him.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，己卯，帝賜懿藥於省中。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on jimao, the emperor bestowed poison upon Yi in the ministry offices.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on jimao, the emperor sent poison to Yi in the ministry compound.

sentences.zh: 懿且死，曰：「家弟在雍，深為朝廷憂之。」

translations.literal: As Yi was about to die, he said: "My younger brother is in Yong—he will be a deep worry to the court."
translations.idiomatic: As he was dying, Yi said: "My brother in Yong will be a grave worry to the court."

sentences.zh: 懿弟侄皆亡匿於里巷，無人發之者；

translations.literal: Yi's younger brothers and nephews all hid in the lanes and alleys; no one reported them;
translations.idiomatic: His brothers and nephews hid in the alleys, and no one betrayed them;

sentences.zh: 唯融捕得，誅之。

translations.literal: only Rong was captured and executed.
translations.idiomatic: only Rong was captured and executed.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，魏以彭城王勰為司徒，錄尚書事；

translations.literal: On dinghai, Wei made Prince Xie of Pengcheng Minister of Works and recorder of the Masters of Writing affairs;
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai, Wei made Prince Xie of Pengcheng minister of works and recorder of the Masters of Writing;

sentences.zh: 勰固辭，不免。

translations.literal: Xie firmly declined but could not escape it.
translations.idiomatic: Xie declined firmly but could not escape the appointment.

sentences.zh: 勰雅好恬素，不樂勢利。

translations.literal: Xie by nature loved quiet simplicity and did not delight in power and profit.
translations.idiomatic: Xie loved quiet simplicity by nature and cared nothing for power or gain.

sentences.zh: 高祖重其事幹，故委以權任，雖有遺詔，復為世宗所留。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu valued his ability in affairs and therefore entrusted him with authority; although there was a dying edict, he was again retained by Emperor Shizong.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu valued his competence and entrusted him with great authority; though the late emperor's will would have released him, Emperor Shizong kept him in office.

sentences.zh: 勰每乖情願，常淒然歎息。

translations.literal: Each time Xie went against his heartfelt wish, he would sigh mournfully.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever his wishes were overruled, he sighed in sorrow.

sentences.zh: 為人美風儀，端嚴若神，折旋合度，出入言笑，觀者忘疲。

translations.literal: As a man his bearing was beautiful, dignified and stern as a spirit; his turns and movements matched measure; going out and in with speech and laughter, viewers forgot weariness.
translations.idiomatic: He was handsome and dignified, every movement measured; his speech and laughter so charmed onlookers that they forgot their fatigue.

sentences.zh: 敦尚文史，物務之暇，披覽不輟。

translations.literal: He earnestly honored literature and history; in the intervals of worldly affairs he opened books and read without cease.
translations.idiomatic: He loved literature and history and read without cease whenever affairs allowed.

sentences.zh: 小心謹慎，初無過失；

translations.literal: Careful and cautious, at first he had no faults;
translations.idiomatic: Careful and cautious, he was never at fault;

sentences.zh: 雖閒居獨處，亦無惰容。

translations.literal: even when at leisure dwelling alone, he had no lazy bearing.
translations.idiomatic: even in private he showed no sign of idleness.

sentences.zh: 愛敬儒雅，傾心禮待。

translations.literal: He loved and respected refined scholars and bent his heart to receive them with ritual courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: He honored scholars and received them with full courtesy.

sentences.zh: 清正儉素，門無私謁。

translations.literal: Upright, clear, frugal, and plain—at his gate there were no private visits.
translations.idiomatic: Upright, frugal, and plain, he accepted no private callers at his gate.

sentences.zh: 十一月，己亥，魏東荊州刺史桓暉入寇，拔下笮戍，歸之者二千餘戶。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on jihai, Wei Eastern Inspector of Jing Province Huan Hui invaded, took the garrison of Xiazuo, and those who submitted numbered more than two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on jihai, Huan Hui, Wei's eastern inspector of Jing Province, invaded, captured the Xiazuo garrison, and won the submission of more than two thousand households.

sentences.zh: 暉，誕之子也。

translations.literal: Hui was the son of Dan.
translations.idiomatic: Hui was a son of Huan Dan.

sentences.zh: 初，帝疑雍州刺史蕭衍有異志。

translations.literal: Earlier, the emperor suspected Inspector of Yong Province Xiao Yan of disloyal intent.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the emperor had suspected Xiao Yan, inspector of Yong Province, of disloyal designs.

sentences.zh: 直後滎陽鄭植弟紹叔為衍寧蠻長史，帝使植以候紹叔為名，往刺衍。

translations.literal: Attendant-after Zheng Zhi of Xingyang's younger brother Shao Shu was Yan's Chief Clerk for Pacifying the Barbarians; the emperor sent Zhi under the pretext of observing Shao Shu to go assassinate Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Zhi of Xingyang, an attendant-after, sent his younger brother Shao Shu—who served Yan as chief clerk for pacifying the barbarians—to assassinate Yan under the pretense of visiting Shao Shu.

sentences.zh: 紹叔知之，密以白衍，衍置酒紹叔家，戲植曰：「朝廷遣卿見圖，今日閒宴，是可取良會也。」

translations.literal: Shao Shu knew it and secretly reported to Yan; Yan set wine at Shao Shu's home and jested to Zhi: "The court sent you to plot against me—today's leisurely feast is a fine occasion to take advantage of."
translations.idiomatic: Shao Shu learned of the plot and secretly informed Yan, who entertained Zhi at Shao Shu's house and jested: "The court sent you to kill me—what better time for a friendly feast than today?

sentences.zh: 賓主大笑。

translations.literal: Host and guest laughed greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Host and guest burst out laughing.

sentences.zh: 又令植歷觀城隍、府庫、士馬、器械、舟艦，植退，謂紹叔曰：「雍州實力，未易圖也。」

translations.literal: He again had Zhi tour the walls and moats, treasuries, soldiers and horses, weapons, and boats and ships; Zhi withdrew and said to Shao Shu: "Yong Province's real strength is not easy to plot against."
translations.idiomatic: Yan then had Zhi inspect the walls, stores, troops, arms, and fleet; when Zhi withdrew he told Shao Shu: "Yong Province is too strong to take lightly."

sentences.zh: 紹叔曰：「兄還，具為天子言之：若取雍州，紹叔請以此眾一戰！」

translations.literal: Shao Shu said: "When brother returns, report fully to the Son of Heaven: if he wishes to take Yong Province, Shao Shu asks to fight one battle with this host!"
translations.idiomatic: Shao Shu said: "Tell the emperor when you return: if he wants Yong Province, I will meet his army in battle with these troops!"

sentences.zh: 送植於南峴，相持慟哭而別。

translations.literal: He sent Zhi off at Nanxian; they held each other and wept bitterly in parting.
translations.idiomatic: He saw Zhi off at Nanxian, and they embraced and wept as they parted.

sentences.zh: 及懿死，衍聞之，夜召張弘策、呂僧珍、長史王茂、別駕柳慶遠、功曹吉士瞻等入宅定議。

translations.literal: When Yi died, Yan heard of it and at night summoned Zhang Hongce, Lu Sengzhen, Chief Clerk Wang Mao, Vice-Prefect Liu Qingyuan, Merit Officer Ji Shizhan, and others into his residence to settle plans.
translations.idiomatic: When Yi died, Yan heard the news and that night summoned Zhang Hongce, Lu Sengzhen, chief clerk Wang Mao, vice-prefect Liu Qingyuan, merit officer Ji Shizhan, and others to his house to decide on a course of action.

sentences.zh: 茂，天生之子；

translations.literal: Mao was the son of Tiansheng;
translations.idiomatic: Mao was a son of Wang Tiansheng;

sentences.zh: 慶遠，元景之弟子也。

translations.literal: Qingyuan was the younger brother's son of Yuanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Qingyuan was a nephew of Liu Yuanjing.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，衍集僚佐謂曰：「昏主暴虐，惡逾於紂，當與卿等共除之！」

translations.literal: On yisi, Yan gathered his staff and said: "The muddled ruler is violent and cruel, his evil exceeding King Zhou's—we should join with you gentlemen to remove him!"
translations.idiomatic: On yisi, Yan assembled his staff and said: "The deranged ruler is more brutal than King Zhou of Shang—we must remove him together!"

sentences.zh: 是日，建牙集眾，得甲士萬餘人，馬千餘匹，船三千艘。

translations.literal: That day he raised the command pennant and gathered the host, obtaining more than ten thousand armored soldiers, more than a thousand horses, and three thousand boats.
translations.idiomatic: That day he raised his banner and mustered more than ten thousand armored men, a thousand horses, and three thousand boats.

sentences.zh: 出檀溪竹木裝艦，葺之以茅，事皆立辦。

translations.literal: He brought out bamboo and timber from Tanxi to fit out the ships, thatched them with straw, and every matter was accomplished on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: Bamboo and timber from Tanxi were used to fit out the fleet and thatched with straw; everything was done at once.

sentences.zh: 諸將爭櫓，呂僧珍出先所具者，每船付二張，爭者乃息。

translations.literal: The generals contended for oars; Lu Sengzhen produced those he had prepared beforehand and gave two to each boat; the disputants then ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The generals quarreled over oars until Lu Sengzhen produced the sets he had prepared in advance and issued two to each boat, ending the dispute.

sentences.zh: 是時，南康王寶融為荊州刺史，西中郎長史蕭穎冑行府州事，帝遣輔國將軍、巴西梓潼二郡太守劉山陽將兵三千之官，就穎冑兵使襲襄陽。

translations.literal: At this time Prince Bao Rong of Nankang was Inspector of Jing Province; Western Central Army Chief Clerk Xiao Yingzhou acted in the provincial and prefectural affairs; the emperor sent General Who Assists the State and Administrator of the two commanderies of Baxi and Zitong, Liu Shanyang, to lead three thousand troops to his post, joining Yingzhou's army to strike Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Prince Bao Rong of Nankang was inspector of Jing Province, with Xiao Yingzhou as acting chief clerk; the emperor sent Liu Shanyang, general who assists the state and administrator of Baxi and Zitong commanderies, with three thousand men to take up his post and join Yingzhou's forces in a surprise attack on Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 衍知其謀，遣參軍王天虎詣江陵，遍與州府書，聲云：「山陽西上，並襲荊、雍。」

translations.literal: Yan knew their plot and sent Army Major Wang Tianhu to Jiangling, writing letters everywhere to the province and prefecture, proclaiming aloud: "Shanyang is going west upriver and will strike both Jing and Yong."
