translations.idiomatic: Yan learned of the plan and sent his aide Wang Tianhu to Jiangling with letters to every office in the province, spreading word that "Shanyang is marching west to attack both Jing and Yong."

sentences.zh: 衍因謂諸將佐曰：「荊州素畏襄陽人，加以脣亡齒寒，寧不暗同邪！

translations.literal: Yan thereupon said to his generals and staff: "Jing Province has always feared the people of Xiangyang; add to that that when the lips perish the teeth grow cold—would they not secretly join!
translations.idiomatic: Yan told his officers: "Jing has always feared Xiangyang, and when the lips are gone the teeth freeze—will they not side with us in secret!

sentences.zh: 我合荊、雍之兵，鼓行而東，雖使韓、白復生，不能為建康計；

translations.literal: If I combine the armies of Jing and Yong and beat drums marching east, even if Han Xin and Bai Qi were reborn, they could not scheme for Jiankang;
translations.idiomatic: If I unite the armies of Jing and Yong and march east with drums beating, not even Han Xin and Bai Qi reborn could save Jiankang;

sentences.zh: 況以昏主役刀敕之徒哉！」

translations.literal: how much more with a muddled ruler employing sword-guard lackeys!"
translations.idiomatic: much less this deranged ruler and his sword-guard thugs!

sentences.zh: 穎冑等得書，疑未能決。

translations.literal: When Yingzhou and the others received the letters, they were suspicious and could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: When Yingzhou received the letters, he hesitated, unable to decide.

sentences.zh: 山陽至巴陵，衍復令天虎繼書與穎冑及其弟南康王龍穎達。

translations.literal: When Shanyang reached Baling, Yan again ordered Tianhu to follow with letters to Yingzhou and his younger brother Prince Long Yingda of Nankang.
translations.idiomatic: When Shanyang reached Baling, Yan sent Tianhu with further letters to Yingzhou and his brother Long Yingda of Nankang.

sentences.zh: 天虎既行，衍謂張弘策曰：「用兵之道，攻心為上。

translations.literal: Once Tianhu had gone, Yan said to Zhang Hongce: "In the way of using troops, attacking the heart is supreme.
translations.idiomatic: After Tianhu left, Yan told Zhang Hongce: "In war, winning hearts comes first.

sentences.zh: 近遣天虎往荊州，人皆有書。

translations.literal: Recently in sending Tianhu to Jing Province, everyone had a letter.
translations.idiomatic: I just sent Tianhu to Jing with a letter for everyone.

sentences.zh: 今段乘驛甚急，止有兩函與行事兄弟，云『天虎口具』；

translations.literal: This time he rides the post relay very urgently; there are only two covers for the acting brothers, saying 'Tianhu will report in person';
translations.idiomatic: This courier ride is very fast; there are only two envelopes for the acting chief and his brother, marked 'details from Tianhu in person';

sentences.zh: 及問天虎而口無所說，天虎是行事心膂，彼間必謂行事與天虎共隱其事，則人人生疑。

translations.literal: when they ask Tianhu and his mouth has nothing to say—Tianhu is the acting chief's trusted core—they there will surely think the acting chief and Tianhu are jointly concealing the affair, and then every person will grow suspicious.
translations.idiomatic: when they question Tianhu and he says nothing, they will think the acting chief and his confidant are hiding something together, and everyone will grow suspicious.

sentences.zh: 山陽惑於眾口，判相嫌貳，則行事進退無以自明，必入吾謀內。

translations.literal: Shanyang will be confused by the crowd's mouths and will certainly grow mutually suspicious; then the acting chief in advance and retreat will have no way to clarify himself and will surely enter within my plan.
translations.idiomatic: Shanyang will be swayed by rumor and turn against them; the acting chief will be unable to clear himself and will fall into my trap.

sentences.zh: 是馳兩空函定一州矣。」

translations.literal: This is to dispatch two empty covers and settle one province."
translations.idiomatic: Thus two empty envelopes will decide a whole province."

sentences.zh: 山陽至江安，遲回十餘日，不上。

translations.literal: Shanyang reached Jiang'an, hesitated and turned back for more than ten days, and did not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Shanyang reached Jiang'an and lingered more than ten days without advancing.

sentences.zh: 穎冑大懼，計無所出，夜遣呼西中郎城局參軍安定席闡文、咨議參軍柳忱，閉齋定議。

translations.literal: Yingzhou was greatly afraid, with no plan to offer; at night he sent to summon Western Central Army City Bureau Major Xi Kanwen of Anding and Adviser Army Major Liu Chen, closed the study, and settled plans.
translations.idiomatic: Yingzhou was terrified and at a loss; that night he summoned Xi Kanwen of Anding, a city bureau major, and Liu Chen, an adviser, and behind closed doors they debated what to do.

sentences.zh: 闡文曰：「蕭雍州蓄養士馬，非復一日。

translations.literal: Kanwen said: "Inspector Xiao of Yong has been gathering soldiers and horses—not for just one day.
translations.idiomatic: Kanwen said: "The inspector of Yong has been building his strength for years.

sentences.zh: 江陵素畏襄陽人，又眾寡不敵，取之必不可制；

translations.literal: Jiangling has always feared the people of Xiangyang, and again the few cannot match the many—taking him would surely be impossible to control;
translations.idiomatic: Jiangling has always feared Xiangyang, and we are too few to overcome him;

sentences.zh: 就能制之，歲寒不為朝廷所容。

translations.literal: even if we could control him, in the year's cold he would not be tolerated by the court.
translations.idiomatic: even if we could defeat him, the court would not tolerate us afterward.

sentences.zh: 今若殺山陽，與雍州舉事，立天子以令諸侯，則霸業成矣！

translations.literal: Now if we kill Shanyang and rise with Yong Province in the affair, establish the Son of Heaven to command the feudal lords—then the hegemonic enterprise is accomplished!
translations.idiomatic: If we kill Shanyang now and rise with Yong, set up an emperor, and command the realm, our great enterprise will succeed!

sentences.zh: 山陽持疑不進，是不信我。

translations.literal: Shanyang holds in doubt and does not advance—this is not trusting us.
translations.idiomatic: Shanyang's hesitation shows he does not trust us.

sentences.zh: 今斬送天虎，則彼疑可釋。

translations.literal: Now if we behead and send Tianhu, then their suspicion can be released.
translations.idiomatic: Behead Tianhu and send his head—that will clear their doubts.

sentences.zh: 至而圖之，罔不濟矣。」

translations.literal: When he arrives and we plot it, nothing will fail to succeed."
translations.idiomatic: When Shanyang arrives, we can carry out the plan—nothing will fail.

sentences.zh: 忱曰：「朝廷狂悖日滋，京師貴人莫不重足累息。

translations.literal: Chen said: "The court grows more mad and perverse by the day; the nobles of the capital all tread with doubled feet and accumulated breaths.
translations.idiomatic: Chen said: "The court grows more deranged every day; the nobles in the capital walk in fear.

sentences.zh: 今幸在遠，得假日自安。

translations.literal: Now we are fortunate to be far away and can borrow days to secure ourselves.
translations.idiomatic: We are fortunate to be far away and can live in peace for now.

sentences.zh: 雍州之事，且藉以相斃耳。

translations.literal: The affair of Yong Province—we may only borrow it to destroy each other.
translations.idiomatic: Let Yong and the court destroy each other—that is enough for us.

sentences.zh: 獨不見蕭令君乎？

translations.literal: Do you alone not see Lord Xiao?
translations.idiomatic: Have you forgotten Lord Xiao?

sentences.zh: 以精兵數千，竟為群邪所陷，禍酷相尋。

translations.literal: With several thousand elite troops, in the end he was trapped by a pack of villains, calamity and cruelty following one after another.
translations.idiomatic: With a few thousand elite troops he was still destroyed by villains, disaster upon disaster.

sentences.zh: 『前事之不忘，後事之師也。』

translations.literal: 'Do not forget past affairs—later affairs take them as teachers.'
translations.idiomatic: 'Past events, not forgotten, are teachers for the future.'

sentences.zh: 且雍州士銳糧多，蕭使君雄姿冠世，必非山陽所能敵。

translations.literal: Moreover Yong Province's soldiers are sharp and grain abundant; Lord Xiao's heroic bearing crowns the age—he is surely not someone Shanyang can match.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Yong's troops are keen and well supplied; Lord Xiao's prowess is unmatched—Shanyang cannot possibly defeat him.

sentences.zh: 若破山陽，荊州復受失律之責，進退無可，宜深慮之。」

translations.literal: If we defeat Shanyang, Jing Province again receives blame for losing discipline; in advance and retreat there is nothing to be done—this should be deeply considered."
translations.idiomatic: If we defeat Shanyang, Jing will bear the blame for the breach; we will have no room to maneuver. Think deeply on this.

sentences.zh: 蕭穎達亦勸穎冑從闡文等計。

translations.literal: Xiao Yingda also urged Yingzhou to follow Kanwen and the others' plan.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yingda also urged Yingzhou to follow Kanwen's plan.

sentences.zh: 詰旦，穎冑謂天虎曰：「卿與劉輔國相識，今不得不借卿頭！」

translations.literal: At dawn, Yingzhou said to Tianhu: "You and Assistant State Liu are acquainted—today I must borrow your head!"
translations.idiomatic: At dawn Yingzhou told Tianhu: "You know Assistant State Liu—I must borrow your head!"

sentences.zh: 乃斬天虎送示山陽，發民車牛，聲雲起步軍征襄陽。

translations.literal: He then beheaded Tianhu and sent it to show Shanyang, mobilized the people's carts and oxen, and proclaimed aloud that the army was setting out to campaign against Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: He beheaded Tianhu and sent the head to Shanyang, mobilized carts and oxen, and announced that the army was marching to attack Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 山陽大喜。

translations.literal: Shanyang was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Shanyang was delighted.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，山陽至江津，單車白服，從左右數十人詣穎冑。

translations.literal: On jiayin, Shanyang reached Jiangjin, came in a single cart in white dress with several tens of attendants, and went to Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin, Shanyang reached Jiangjin and came to Yingzhou in a single cart dressed in white, with only a few dozen attendants.

sentences.zh: 穎冑使前汶陽太守劉孝慶等伏兵城內，山陽入門，即於車中斬之。

translations.literal: Yingzhou had the former Administrator of Wenyang, Liu Xiaoqing, and others lie in ambush inside the city; when Shanyang entered the gate, they at once beheaded him in the cart.
translations.idiomatic: Yingzhou had Liu Xiaoqing, the former administrator of Wenyang, and others wait in ambush inside the city; the moment Shanyang entered the gate they cut off his head in the cart.

sentences.zh: 副軍主李無履收餘眾請降。

translations.literal: Deputy Army Commander Li Wulü gathered the remaining crowd and requested surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Li Wulü, the deputy commander, gathered the remaining troops and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 柳忱，世隆之子也。

translations.literal: Liu Chen was the son of Shilong.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Chen was a son of Liu Shilong.

sentences.zh: 穎冑慮西中郎司馬夏侯詳不同，以告忱，忱曰：「易耳！

translations.literal: Yingzhou worried that Western Central Army Marshal Xiahou Xiang would not agree; he told Chen; Chen said: "Easy!
translations.idiomatic: Yingzhou feared that Xiahou Xiang, the western central army marshal, would not agree; he told Chen, who said, "That is easy!

sentences.zh: 近詳求婚，未之許也。」

translations.literal: Recently Xiang sought marriage—I have not yet granted it."
translations.idiomatic: He recently asked for a marriage alliance, which I have not yet granted."

sentences.zh: 乃以女嫁詳子夔，而告之謀，詳從之。

translations.literal: He then gave his daughter in marriage to Xiang's son Kui, told him the plot, and Xiang followed it.
translations.idiomatic: He gave his daughter to Xiang's son Kui, revealed the plot, and Xiang agreed.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，以南康王寶融教纂嚴，又教赦囚徒，施惠澤，頒賞格。

translations.literal: On yimao, through Prince Bao Rong of Nankang an order was issued to tighten discipline, another order to amnesty prisoners, bestow favors, and promulgate reward standards.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao, through Prince Bao Rong of Nankang orders were issued to tighten discipline, amnesty prisoners, grant favors, and publish reward scales.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，以蕭衍為使持節都督前鋒諸軍事。

translations.literal: On bingchen, Xiao Yan was made bearer of the staff and commander of all vanguard military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen, Xiao Yan was made bearer of the staff and commander of all vanguard forces.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，以蕭穎冑為都督行留諸軍事。

translations.literal: On dingsi, Xiao Yingzhou was made commander of all military affairs acting and remaining in place.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi, Xiao Yingzhou was appointed commander of all forces in the field and in garrison.

sentences.zh: 穎冑有器局，既舉大事，慮心委己，眾情歸之。

translations.literal: Yingzhou had capacity and vision; once he had raised the great affair, he devoted his mind and entrusted himself, and the crowd's hearts turned to him.
translations.idiomatic: Yingzhou had talent and vision; once the revolt began he gave himself wholly to it, and the army rallied to him.

sentences.zh: 以別駕南陽宗夬及同郡中兵參軍劉坦、咨議參軍樂藹為州人所推信，軍府經略，每事諮焉。

translations.literal: He took Vice-Prefect Zong Yan of Nanyang and Central Army Major Liu Tan of the same commandery and Adviser Army Major Yue Ai as men the province trusted and pushed forward; for the army headquarters' strategy, on every matter he consulted them.
translations.idiomatic: He relied on Zong Yan of Nanyang, the vice-prefect, Liu Tan, a central army major from the same commandery, and Yue Ai, an adviser—men trusted throughout the province—and consulted them on every military decision.

sentences.zh: 穎冑、夬各獻私錢穀及換借富貲以助軍。

translations.literal: Yingzhou and Yan each contributed private money and grain and borrowed from the wealthy to aid the army.
translations.idiomatic: Yingzhou and Yan each contributed their private funds and grain and borrowed from the wealthy to support the army.

sentences.zh: 長法寺僧素富，鑄黃金為龍數千兩埋土中。

translations.literal: The monks of Changfa Temple had long been wealthy; they cast gold into dragons numbering several thousand taels and buried them in the earth.
translations.idiomatic: The monks of Changfa Temple were wealthy and had cast several thousand taels of gold into dragon figures and buried them in the ground.

sentences.zh: 穎冑取之，以充軍費。

translations.literal: Yingzhou took them and used them to fill military expenses.
translations.idiomatic: Yingzhou seized them to pay for the army.

sentences.zh: 穎冑遣使送劉山陽首於蕭衍，且言年月未利，當須明年二月進兵。

translations.literal: Yingzhou sent envoys to deliver Liu Shanyang's head to Xiao Yan, and also said the year and month were not favorable and that troops should advance only in the second month of next year.
translations.idiomatic: Yingzhou sent Liu Shanyang's head to Xiao Yan and proposed waiting until the second month of the coming year to march, saying the calendar was not yet favorable.

sentences.zh: 衍曰：「舉事之初，所藉者一時驍銳之心。

translations.literal: Yan said: "At the beginning of raising the affair, what one relies on is the moment's fierce and sharp hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Yan replied: "At the start of a rising, one depends on the army's immediate fighting spirit.

sentences.zh: 事事相接，猶恐疑怠；

translations.literal: Affairs follow one upon another—one still fears doubt and slackness;
translations.idiomatic: One event follows another, and even then men grow doubtful and slack;

sentences.zh: 若頓兵十旬，必生悔吝。

translations.literal: if you halt the army for a hundred days, regret and stinginess will surely arise.
translations.idiomatic: halt the army a hundred days and regret is sure to follow.

sentences.zh: 且坐甲十萬，糧用自竭；

translations.literal: Moreover, sitting with a hundred thousand armor, grain and supplies will exhaust themselves;
translations.idiomatic: A hundred thousand men under arms will exhaust their supplies;

sentences.zh: 若童子立異，則大事不成。

translations.literal: if a child stands apart with difference, then the great affair will not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: if some boy stirs up trouble, the whole enterprise will fail.

sentences.zh: 況處分已定，安可中息哉！

translations.literal: How much more when dispositions are already settled—how could one pause midway!
translations.idiomatic: And our plans are already set—how can we stop halfway!

sentences.zh: 昔武王伐紂，行逆太歲，豈復待年月乎！」

translations.literal: In the past King Wu campaigned against King Zhou, marching against the Tai Sui star—did he again wait for year and month!"
translations.idiomatic: When King Wu attacked King Zhou of Shang, he marched against the astrological sign of the year—did he wait for a favorable calendar!"

sentences.zh: 戊午，衍上表勸南康王寶融稱尊號；

translations.literal: On wuwu, Yan submitted a memorial urging Prince Bao Rong of Nankang to assume the exalted title;
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu, Yan memorialized urging Prince Bao Rong of Nankang to take the imperial title;

sentences.zh: 不許。

translations.literal: it was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: again he refused.

sentences.zh: 十二月，穎冑與夏侯詳移檄建康百官及州郡牧守，數帝及梅蟲兒、茹法珍罪惡。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Yingzhou and Xiahou Xiang issued a proclamation to the hundred officials of Jiankang and the provincial and commandery guardians and magistrates, recounting the emperor's and Mei Chong'er's and Ru Fazhen's crimes and evils.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, Yingzhou and Xiahou Xiang issued a proclamation to the officials of Jiankang and to governors throughout the realm, denouncing the emperor and his favorites Mei Chong'er and Ru Fazhen.

sentences.zh: 穎冑遣冠軍將軍天水楊公則向湘州，西中郎參軍南郡鄧元起向夏口。

translations.literal: Yingzhou sent Champion General Yang Gongze of Tianshui toward Xiang Province and Western Central Army Major Deng Yuanqi of Nan commandery toward Xiakou.
translations.idiomatic: Yingzhou sent Yang Gongze of Tianshui, champion general, against Xiang Province and Deng Yuanqi of Nan commandery, a western central army major, against Xiakou.

sentences.zh: 軍主王法度坐不進軍免官。

translations.literal: Army Commander Wang Fadu was deprived of office for the crime of not advancing the army.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Fadu, an army commander, was dismissed for failing to advance.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，荊州將佐復勸寶融稱尊號；

translations.literal: On yihai, Jing Province's generals and aides again urged Bao Rong to assume the exalted title;
translations.idiomatic: On yihai, the officers of Jing Province again urged Bao Rong to take the imperial title;

sentences.zh: 不許。

translations.literal: it was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: again he refused.

sentences.zh: 夏侯詳之子驍騎將軍但為殿中主帥，詳密召之，但自建康亡歸。

translations.literal: Xiahou Xiang's son, General of Agile Cavalry Dan, was chief commander in the palace hall; Xiang secretly summoned him, and Dan fled from Jiankang and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Xiahou Xiang's son Dan, a general of agile cavalry and palace commander, was secretly summoned by his father and fled Jiankang to join him.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，至江陵，稱奉德皇太后之令：「南康王宜纂承皇祚，方俟清宮，未即大號；

translations.literal: On renchen, he reached Jiangling and proclaimed that he followed Empress Dowager De's order: "Prince Bao Rong of Nankang ought to succeed to the imperial fortune; he is still awaiting the cleansing of the palace and is not yet to take the great title;
translations.idiomatic: On renchen he reached Jiangling and announced an order in the name of Empress Dowager De: "Prince Bao Rong of Nankang should succeed to the throne, but must wait until the palace is secured before taking the imperial title;

sentences.zh: 可封十郡為宣城王、相國、荊州牧，加黃鉞，選百官，西中郎府、南康國如故。

translations.literal: he may be enfeoffed with ten commanderies as Prince of Xuancheng, Chancellor of State, and Governor of Jing Province, with the yellow battle-axe added, selecting the hundred offices; the Western Central Army headquarters and the state of Nankang remain as before.
translations.idiomatic: for now he may be made prince of Xuancheng over ten commanderies, chancellor of state, and governor of Jing Province, with the yellow battle-axe, authority to appoint officials, while the western central army headquarters and the state of Nankang remain unchanged.

sentences.zh: 須軍次近路，主者備法駕奉迎。」

translations.literal: When the army reaches the near road, the responsible officials shall prepare the imperial equipage to welcome him."
translations.idiomatic: When the army approaches, the responsible officials shall prepare the imperial equipage to welcome him."

sentences.zh: 竟陵太守新野曹景宗遣親人說蕭衍，迎南康王都襄陽，先正尊號，然後將軍；

translations.literal: Administrator of Jingling, Cao Jingzong of Xinye, sent a close associate to persuade Xiao Yan to welcome Prince Bao Rong of Nankang to establish the capital at Xiangyang, first set the exalted title right, and then act as general;
translations.idiomatic: Cao Jingzong of Xinye, administrator of Jingling, sent an envoy urging Xiao Yan to bring Prince Bao Rong to Xiangyang as capital, proclaim him emperor first, and then serve as his general;

sentences.zh: 衍不從。

translations.literal: Yan did not follow this.
translations.idiomatic: Yan refused.

sentences.zh: 王茂私謂張弘策曰：「今以南康置人手中，彼扶天子以令諸侯，節下前進為人所使，此豈它日之長計乎！」

translations.literal: Wang Mao privately said to Zhang Hongce: "Now if Nankang is placed in another's hands, he will support the Son of Heaven to command the feudal lords; my lord advancing will be used by others—is this a long-term plan for other days!"
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mao told Zhang Hongce privately: "If we put Nankang in another man's hands, he will hold the emperor and command the lords—you will march at another's orders. Is that a plan for the long term?

sentences.zh: 弘策以告衍，衍曰：「若前塗大事不捷，故自蘭艾同焚；

translations.literal: Hongce reported this to Yan; Yan said: "If on the road ahead the great affair does not succeed, then of old orchid and mugwort burn together;
translations.idiomatic: Hongce reported this to Yan, who said: "If we fail, we perish together like orchid and mugwort in the fire;

sentences.zh: 若其克捷，則威振四海，誰敢不從，豈碌碌受人處分者邪！」

translations.literal: if it succeeds, then authority will shake the four seas—who would dare not follow—how could one be a mediocrity who accepts others' dispositions!"
translations.idiomatic: if we succeed, our authority will awe the realm—who would dare disobey—would I be a man who takes orders from others!"

sentences.zh: 初，陳顯達、崔慧景之亂，人心不安。

translations.literal: Earlier, during the disorders of Chen Xianda and Cui Huijing, people's hearts were unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, during the revolts of Chen Xianda and Cui Huijing, the realm was uneasy.

sentences.zh: 或問時事於上庸太守杜陵韋睿，睿曰：陳雖舊將，非命世才；

translations.literal: Someone asked about current affairs of Wei Rui of Duling, Administrator of Shangyong; Rui said: "Chen, though an old general, is not a talent fated for the age;
translations.idiomatic: When someone asked Wei Rui of Duling, administrator of Shangyong, about the situation, Rui said: "Chen is an old soldier but no man of destiny;

sentences.zh: 崔頗更事，懦而不武；

translations.literal: Cui has considerable experience in affairs, but is timid and not martial;
translations.idiomatic: Cui has seen much service but is timid and no warrior;

sentences.zh: 其赤族宜矣。

translations.literal: that their clans were exterminated to the root was fitting."
translations.idiomatic: it was fitting that their clans were destroyed."

sentences.zh: 定天下者，殆必在吾州將乎？」

translations.literal: The one who will settle the realm is probably surely among the generals of our province, is he not?"
translations.idiomatic: The man who will settle the realm is surely among our province's generals, is he not?

sentences.zh: 乃遣二子自結於蕭衍。

translations.literal: He thereupon sent his two sons to bind themselves to Xiao Yan on their own.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent his two sons to pledge themselves to Xiao Yan.

sentences.zh: 及衍起兵，睿帥郡兵二千倍道赴之。

translations.literal: When Yan raised troops, Rui led two thousand commandery soldiers by double marches to hurry to him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan rose in arms, Rui marched two thousand commandery troops to join him at forced pace.

sentences.zh: 華山太守藍田康絢帥郡兵三千赴衍。

translations.literal: Administrator of Huashan, Kang Xuan of Lantian, led three thousand commandery troops to go to Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Kang Xuan of Lantian, administrator of Huashan, brought three thousand commandery troops to Yan.

sentences.zh: 馮道根時居母喪，聞衍起兵，帥鄉人子弟勝兵者悉往赴之。

translations.literal: Feng Daogen was at that time in mourning for his mother; hearing Yan had raised troops, he led the fellows of his township, younger kinsmen, and all fit for arms to hurry to join him.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Daogen was in mourning for his mother, but when he heard Yan had risen, he led every able-bodied man from his township to join him.

sentences.zh: 梁、南秦二州刺史柳惔亦起兵應衍。

translations.literal: The Inspector of the two provinces of Liang and South Qin, Liu Yan, also raised troops in response to Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yan, inspector of Liang and South Qin provinces, also rose in support of Yan.

sentences.zh: 惔，忱之兄也。

translations.literal: Yan was the elder brother of Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was the elder brother of Liu Chen.

sentences.zh: 帝聞劉山陽死，發詔討荊、雍。

translations.literal: The emperor heard that Liu Shanyang was dead and issued an edict to campaign against Jing and Yong.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard that Liu Shanyang was dead, he issued an edict to campaign against Jing and Yong.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，以冠軍長史劉澮為雍州刺史；

translations.literal: On wuyin, Champion Chief Clerk Liu Hui was made Inspector of Yong Province;
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin, Liu Hui, champion chief clerk, was appointed inspector of Yong Province;

sentences.zh: 遣驍騎將軍薛元嗣、制局監暨榮伯將兵及過糧百四十餘船送郢州刺史張沖，使拒西師。

translations.literal: he sent General of Agile Cavalry Xue Yuansi and Bureau Supervisor Ji Rongbo to lead troops and more than a hundred and forty grain boats in passage to deliver to Inspector of Ying Province Zhang Chong, to make them resist the western army.
translations.idiomatic: and sent Xue Yuansi, general of agile cavalry, and Ji Rongbo, a bureau supervisor, with troops and more than 140 grain ships to reinforce Zhang Chong, inspector of Ying Province, against the western army.

sentences.zh: 元嗣等懲劉山陽之死，疑沖，不敢進，停夏口浦；

translations.literal: Yuansi and the others, taking warning from Liu Shanyang's death, suspected Chong and did not dare advance, halting at Xiakou ford;
translations.idiomatic: Yuansi and his men, mindful of Shanyang's fate, distrusted Chong and halted at Xiakou without advancing;

sentences.zh: 聞西師將至，乃相帥入郢城。

translations.literal: hearing the western army was about to arrive, they then led one another into Ying city.
translations.idiomatic: when they heard the western army was approaching, they withdrew together into Ying city.

sentences.zh: 前竟陵太守房僧寄將還建康，至郢，帝敕僧寄留守魯山，除驍騎將軍。

translations.literal: The former Administrator of Jingling, Fang Sengji, was about to return to Jiankang; when he reached Ying, the emperor ordered Sengji to remain and guard Lushan and made him General of Agile Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Sengji, the former administrator of Jingling, was returning to Jiankang; when he reached Ying, the emperor ordered him to hold Lushan and made him general of agile cavalry.

sentences.zh: 張沖與之結盟，遣軍主孫樂祖將數千人助僧寄守魯山。

translations.literal: Zhang Chong formed an alliance with him and sent Army Commander Sun Lezu to lead several thousand men to help Sengji guard Lushan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chong allied with him and sent Sun Lezu, an army commander, with several thousand men to help defend Lushan.

sentences.zh: 蕭穎冑與武寧太守鄧元起書，招之。

translations.literal: Xiao Yingzhou wrote to Wuning Administrator Deng Yuanqi to recruit him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yingzhou wrote to Deng Yuanqi, administrator of Wuning, inviting him to join.

sentences.zh: 張沖待元起素厚，眾皆勸其還郢，元起大言於眾曰：「朝廷暴虐，誅戮宰輔，群小用事，衣冠道盡。

translations.literal: Zhang Chong had always treated Yuanqi thickly; the crowd all urged him to return to Ying; Yuanqi spoke loudly to the crowd, saying: "The court is violent and cruel, executes and kills chief ministers, petty men hold power, and the way of the gentry and officials is exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chong had always treated Yuanqi well, and many urged him to return to Ying; Yuanqi declared to them: "The court is brutal, slaughtering its ministers; petty men rule, and civilized order is dead.

sentences.zh: 荊、雍二州同舉大事，何患不克！

translations.literal: Jing and Yong, the two provinces, jointly raise the great affair—what worry that we will not overcome!
translations.idiomatic: Jing and Yong have risen together—how can we fail!

sentences.zh: 且我老母在西，若事不成，正受戮昏朝，倖免不孝之罪。」

translations.literal: Moreover my old mother is in the west; if the affair does not succeed, I will just receive execution from the muddled court and by luck escape the crime of unfilial conduct."
translations.idiomatic: My old mother is in the west; if we fail, I will die at the hands of this deranged court and be spared the shame of unfilial conduct."

sentences.zh: 即日治嚴上道，至江陵，為西中郎中兵參軍。

translations.literal: That same day he put his baggage in order and took the road; reaching Jiangling, he became Western Central Army Central Army Major.
translations.idiomatic: That same day he set out; reaching Jiangling, he was made central army major of the western central army.

sentences.zh: 湘州行事張寶積發兵自守，未知所附。

translations.literal: Acting head of Xiang Province Zhang Baoji raised troops to guard himself, not knowing whom to follow.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Baoji, acting head of Xiang Province, mobilized troops to hold his ground, uncertain which side to join.

sentences.zh: 楊公則克巴陵，進軍白沙，寶積懼，請降，公則入長沙，撫納之。

translations.literal: Yang Gongze took Baling, advanced his army to Baisha; Baoji was afraid and requested surrender; Gongze entered Changsha and comforted and accepted him.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Gongze took Baling and advanced to Baisha; Baoji, frightened, surrendered; Gongze entered Changsha and pacified the region.

sentences.zh: 是歲，北秦州刺史楊集始將眾萬餘自漢中北出，規復舊地。

translations.literal: This year, Inspector of North Qin Province Yang Jishi led a crowd of more than ten thousand from Hanzhong northward out, planning to recover his old territory.
translations.idiomatic: That year Yang Jishi, inspector of North Qin Province, led more than ten thousand men north from Hanzhong to recover his former territory.

sentences.zh: 魏梁州刺史楊椿將步騎五千出頓下辯，遺集始書，開以利害，集始遂復將其部曲千餘人降魏。

translations.literal: Wei Inspector of Liang Province Yang Chun led five thousand foot and horse out to encamp at Xiabian, sent Jishi a letter explaining advantage and harm, and Jishi thereupon again led his personal troops of more than a thousand to surrender to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Chun, Wei's inspector of Liang Province, marched five thousand infantry and cavalry to Xiabian and wrote to Jishi setting out the costs and benefits; Jishi then led his thousand-odd followers back to surrender to Wei.

sentences.zh: 魏人還其爵位，使歸守武興。

translations.literal: The people of Wei restored his rank and title and sent him back to guard Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Wei restored his titles and sent him back to guard Wuxing.
